Sports.title: FIA admits F1's ADUO system has "weaknesses" – but defends its measurements
Sports.content:
Few topics in the Formula 1 paddock have generated as much political debate during the first half of the season as ADUO, the Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities.

The system was introduced as a safety net for a manufacturer that falls behind, partly in response to Honda's situation under the previous regulations, but in practice it has turned into a political battleground.

Toto Wolff immediately warned that it should not become a "leapfrog mechanism", although there was considerable surprise when it was not Mercedes High Performance Powertrains but Red Bull Ford Powertrains that ended up at the top of the FIA's first ranking.

There are two reasons for this. Firstly, the ADUO measurements are based solely on the internal combustion engine, creating a significant discrepancy between the measurement method and the development opportunities, which also cover the electrical side of the power unit.

Secondly, there have been suggestions in the paddock that several manufacturers – including Mercedes and Ferrari – played the game cleverly by not showing their full hand during the opening race weekends in order to secure one ADUO token, or even two in Ferrari's case.

The outcome of the first period has caused frustration at Red Bull, which also explains why those results have still not been publicly announced.

Red Bull Ford Powertrains has been placed at the top of the standings by the FIA following the first measurement period, much to the frustration of Red Bull’s top management Photo by: Mark Thompson / Getty Images

FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis previously indicated that he was open to considering more parameters for the ADUO measurements – such as the size of the turbo – but that teams and manufacturers pushed to keep the system as simple as possible.

That raises the question of whether the FIA has been surprised by all the controversy surrounding ADUO this season, which Autosport asked Tombazis.

"Well, in F1 it seems that almost everything is quite sensitive. So it's very rare that you get 11 teams and five or six PU manufacturers saying, 'Fantastic, we all agree'," the Greek replied.

"The only thing I think that everybody agrees on is that the August shutdown is a good thing, and I have to remind you that it was my idea.

"But that's the only thing that everybody agrees on. I think everything else [is difficult]. And even that took time for everybody to agree on. You know, when Franz Tost was still in place, he didn't want it."

According to Tombazis, two different aspects need to be distinguished when assessing ADUO: how accurate the measurements are and whether the system is working as originally intended.

Amid all the dissatisfaction surrounding the outcome of period one, Red Bull requested a factual verification of the results, but according to Tombazis, the FIA's measurements have proven to be accurate.

"Everything is quite sensitive because everyone is so competitive and so focused on their relative position compared to the others. So yes, it has been quite a challenge," he continued.

"I think our measurement, in my opinion, has proven to be very accurate. With that said, has everything worked fine? No, because obviously people are not happy and so on. Do we need to think about improvements in the future? Yes, I would say so."

Tombazis acknowledges that the system may need changes in the coming years, but insists that the measurements are correct Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

One of the apparent flaws is that the other manufacturers could effectively put Red Bull in checkmate. If they continue playing the game and do not use the tokens they have been awarded to develop the internal combustion engine, they could theoretically keep Red Bull at the top of the ranking for longer.

Tombazis, however, does not believe things will go that far in practice: "Well, I don't think it would be convenient for you to always be below [your maximum power] just to keep getting more opportunities, because then what's the point of opportunities if it isn't ultimately for you to be on top?"

That said, the 58-year-old admits that the system needs a rethink for the coming years: "I think the system is working as it was designed, but I do think there are some weaknesses that we need to address in the future. Also to make it less time-consuming and less controversial, we do need to make some steps to improve it in the future."

One logical suggestion would be to consider the entire power unit in the measurements rather than just the ICE, but Tombazis does not want to discuss specific ideas at this stage.

ADUO works for Honda, but does it work for F1 as a whole?

Honda will introduce its first ADUO upgrade at Zandvoort and states that the system works well for the manufacturer that needs it most Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

Honda is naturally the manufacturer with the largest deficit and is therefore the clearest example of what ADUO was originally designed for.

General trackside manager and chief engineer Shintaro Orihara says the system does work for Honda, although he is open to a rethink in the longer term for the benefit of the championship as a whole.

"I think the number we received from the FIA looks reasonable. I would say that number is fair. And also, thanks to ADUO, we are now working hard to develop our engine," Orihara told Autosport.

"So, at this moment, it's difficult to say if the ADUO system is working correctly [or not]. But, at least for Honda, we have the maximum chance to develop our engine thanks to the ADUO system.

"Maybe we adjust [things after] monitoring how the ADUO system works for Formula 1. It is working well for Honda, but we need to keep monitoring how that works for all manufacturers. It should be fair. At this moment, it looks fair for Honda, but we need to keep monitoring it."

Sports.title: What to expect from Honda's long-awaited F1 power unit upgrade
Sports.content:
While Aston Martin introduced its first major upgrade package for the AMR26 in Hungary, Honda will bring its first update of the 2026 Formula 1 season to Zandvoort.

With Adrian Newey’s first upgrade package of the year, the deficit on the chassis side has been reduced considerably. Aston Martin is still a long way from where it wants to be, but figures from Paceteq show that its deficit in terms of race pace was “just” 2.034 seconds per lap in Hungary.

During the preceding weekends at Silverstone and Spa, that deficit was still more than five seconds per lap, although there are two important caveats. Firstly, both iconic circuits are much longer, while the Hungaroring is also less dependent on power unit performance.

The latter remains a weakness for Aston Martin, although Honda hopes to make a step forward at the start of the second half of the season with its first ADUO upgrade of the year.

That upgrade is entirely focused on the internal combustion engine, which general trackside manager and chief engineer Shintaro Orihara still identifies as Honda's biggest weakness compared to the competition.

"Our engine performance is definitely poor compared to other manufacturers. So probably the most important point to improve now is our engine performance because, as I mentioned, the gap is quite huge.

Shintaro Orihara, Trackside General Manager and Chief Engineer of Honda Racing Corporation Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"Without improving our combustion engine performance, [the rest doesn’t help]. Let's say, if we improve energy management, that doesn't help if the engine performance is poor," Orihara explained during an exclusive interview with Autosport.

"So now we purely focus on improving our engine performance. Once we achieve our target there, then maybe we can optimise some other small areas. But still our main focus point is the engine performance, the combustion engine."

Honda knows that closing the deficit in terms of outright power will take time, meaning further upgrades will be required after this first step – with some of the most optimistic estimates suggesting a gain of up to 30bhp.

When asked about the specific target for the Zandvoort upgrade, Orihara outlines an objective similar to Aston Martin's in Hungary: getting back to what is referred to as the "racing field".

That has been achieved on the chassis side, but Orihara stresses that the same needs to happen on the power unit side.

"Our target is to get back to the racing field, to a situation where the 10 milliseconds or 20 milliseconds that we try so hard to find every weekend, can actually make a difference."

Lance Stroll, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: James Sutton / Formula 1 / Formula Motorsport Ltd via Getty Images

Honda faces fresh driveability challenge with new engine

Because the power unit is undergoing significant changes, the Zandvoort upgrade also brings another question mark. It concerns a term that has been discussed frequently during the opening months of this F1 season: drivability, the feeling the drivers get from the power unit.

"We developed our tools to optimise our driveability. We have made good progress and we were close to what we wanted to achieve," Orihara said.

"But when we introduce the spec 2 engine, the combustion characteristics will change significantly. Well, maybe not significantly, but there will be a big difference.

"And then engine behaviour will be changed in the cornering phase as well. So yeah, we need to develop our driveability again."

It goes hand in hand with Aston Martin's upgrades on the chassis side, which also have an impact on the drivability of the power unit.

"With the car spec changing, cornering speeds will be much higher. And then demands on driveability will be changing as well."

Lance Stroll, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

It sounds as though Honda will face the same drivability challenge it encountered at the start of this year, but Orihara stresses that the Japanese manufacturer will not be back to square one under any circumstances. After all, the lessons learned can still be applied to the new specification.

"There has been big progress through this first half of the season. We developed our optimised way [for drivability]," he said.

"We will introduce our new engine and probably we need [to do] more work to improve driveability again, but now we know how we need to do it and where we should improve.

"That has been a big learning, and we can carry over that learning point to our B spec engine."

It is partly because of this aspect – working on drivability – that Aston Martin's recent filming day at the Hungaroring with the new power unit was so important. It has already provided both parties with some initial data to analyse, helping them avoid unpleasant surprises at Zandvoort.

Sports.title: How Cadillac is ‘building its plane while flying in it’ in F1
Sports.content:
Cadillac Formula 1 team principal Graeme Lowdon has given an update on the outfit’s current infrastructure, which is still being developed.

F1’s newest squad operates from several locations, mainly its Silverstone hub, while it makes the most of General Motors facilities in North Carolina and Michigan, and uses Toyota’s wind tunnel in Cologne.

Cadillac has been building a new F1 factory in Fishers, in the Indianapolis suburbs, while its power unit department will be based in the Charlotte area where the parent company is already based.

Meanwhile, the team keeps chasing its first Q2 appearance and maiden world championship points.

“We're still building,” Lowdon said. “It's building the plane while flying in it, or the ship while we're sailing in it. We are still doing that. We're still building factories.

“Next to my desk are some steel toecap boots and a hard hat, and we go and look at construction sites. A very, very big one in Indianapolis, and then a smaller one in Silverstone. And obviously the PU company is building the factory down in Charlotte as well.

Cadillac F1 Team works shop in Silverstone Photo by: Cadillac Communications

“We're still recruiting like mad as well, and so there's still an awful lot of building going on. And then Q2 of this year has kind of allowed us to start understanding the strengths and weaknesses of the MAC-26 as well, and also the strengths and weaknesses of the team operationally.

“We like to say every day is a school day. If it's a day where we haven't learned something, it's a day we've wasted. And so we're just trying to find every area that we can improve and constantly, constantly improve.

“And at the minute, it's big chunks because there's just so much to do and there's so much that's new as well. And so we're somewhere off that area where you're just refining things, where I think a lot of the other teams are probably more in that mode.”

As far as the Fishers factory is concerned, Lowdon hinted at “more announcements soon about when various things will come online”, with the new simulator “going in as we speak”.

“It's still in construction at the moment,” the Briton explained. “It'll be phased, because it's 450,000 square feet. It's not small.”

Asked if things would start next year at Fishers, Lowdon replied: “In broad terms, yes. It's very well advanced, the whole construction there, but it's a huge project.

“There's a lot happening and coming online at Silverstone as well.”

Sports.title: Why McLaren won't switch full focus to its 2027 car anytime soon
Sports.content:
Having started the 2026 season on the back foot, McLaren is showing signs of what made this iteration of the storied team so successful in the first place over the past two years.

True to its successful strike rate with in-season upgrades in 2024 and 2025, McLaren's latest upgrade package in Hungary, featuring a revised floor and the latest iteration of its front wing, was another significant step forward building on previous updates in Miami and Montreal. It gave its drivers a chance to fight for victory, with Lando Norris claiming his and the team's first grand prix win of the campaign.

McLaren's race-winning form has yet to be confirmed on different circuits and in varying weather conditions. But it has likely come too late to successfully defend either championship, with the team still 159 points behind leader Mercedes. In the drivers' championship Norris is still only fifth after losing a lot of ground during a difficult opening spell of the campaign, with Piastri further behind in seventh.

The team explained its sluggish start to the 2026 season was down to it having to fend off a late title challenge from Red Bull's Max Verstappen last year, combined with a course correction it made during the development of its 2026 concept.

"We obviously had a big, although slightly surprising, competition with Max at the end of the season," said Neil Houldey, McLaren's technical director for engineering. "But obviously, we were developing our car right until the end of the year whilst working on 2026. When you look at how we went into the start of 2026, we were a little bit on the back foot compared with a couple of teams.

"I think we've done a pretty good job of bringing a lot of upgrades that have added performance to the car. We've put ourselves in a better position from a PU perspective, from a car perspective. But you'd have to say that a couple of teams out there have certainly done a better job than us. And now we've got to find a way in this back half of the season to outdevelop them and become a little bit more competitive at more races."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Oscar Piastri, McLaren Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

Rather than last year, when the likes of Ferrari and other teams out of contention resolutely switched focus to the following season early, McLaren still feels adding performance to this year's car will stand it in good stead in 2027. That's despite its car design itself not fully carrying over, as the team is already plotting a 2027 challenger with a longer wheelbase and a changed suspension layout.

There are also a number of tweaks to the regulations next year, including the front bib or tea tray at the front of the floor becoming 300mm shorter, which will not only impact downforce generation but also ride heights.

"We expect the next few races to be bringing some major parts, and we expect to do that quite late on into the season as well," Houldey confirmed. "We're certainly not stopping development on ‘26 because we know that whatever we take from 2026 into 2027, that learning will carry over.

"Even if our car might get a little bit longer, even if conceptually the suspension might change, everything that we're learning this year is very much relevant for next year. So, we're very keen to keep developing the car for as long as we possibly can."

He added: "The best way to understand the performance you're generating is by putting it on the track and actually properly testing it and making sure it does what you expect it to do. If you stop 2026 now, it certainly puts you more into that theoretical world, and it doesn't necessarily mean that you'll generate lots and lots of 2027 performance.

"So, our view at the moment is there's so many races coming up that we can add performance to. Let's find ways of adding performance to those at those events, and we know that that learning will be useful for 2027."

Oscar Piastri, McLaren Photo by: Steven Tee / LAT Images via Getty Images

Like every other team, McLaren has been able to take inspiration from what its rivals are doing, with the squad the third team to trial an upside-down rear wing first seen on the 2026 Ferrari in winter testing.

Houldey admitted the team was a little "disappointed" it had missed that opportunity in the regulations. But the innovation seen at Ferrari further underlines how the 2026 technical regulations are less prescriptive than perhaps first assumed.

"Aerodynamically, although [the cars] look quite close, I think they're not, actually," Houldey explained. "There's a little bit that people have opened up. I think the regulations give us enough freedom.

"When you're talking about year one, you really pick up a lot that other teams have done. You pick up a lot within the regulations when you re-read them that actually means that they're a little bit more open than 2022 to 2025, and obviously in that first year, you learn so much that it's good fun to be able to look at different concepts.

"Sidepods are a good example where maybe there isn't a huge amount of performance in them, but you see so much down pitlane that are different. No one's converged yet, so you've got a lot of things that you can try out to find the right direction."

Sports.title: FIA wants F1 cars to lose another 80kg under next rules overhaul
Sports.content:
When the 2026 Formula 1 rules were introduced, the FIA frequently spoke about the so-called "nimble car concept".

The machinery was supposed to become smaller and lighter, although it has to be said that the changes are still relatively marginal. The wheelbase is 20cm shorter this year, while the new cars are also 10cm narrower.

The minimum weight has been set at 768kg, a reduction of 32kg compared to last season. Together with significantly less downforce – which means drivers once again wrestle the steering wheel more and the cars look less like they are running on rails – the main objectives have been achieved.

However, there has barely been any discussion about that during the first eight months of the year, as everything has been overshadowed by complaints about the power units and energy management.

But on the chassis side, FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis does believe that the new set of regulations represents a step forward.

"I think probably yes, although one should never assume that the job is finished. But I do think cars follow each other more closely," Tombazis told select media including Autosport.

According to the FIA, the effect of dirty air has been reduced to the level seen during the first year under the previous ruleset. Tombazis is confident that this time teams will be less able to throw a spanner in the works with clever solutions that undermine the spirit of the regulations.

"I believe we are similar to where we were at the start of the 2022 championship, but I think it's a bit more robust this year," he continued.

Tombazis emphasises that, on the chassis side, the 2026 machinery still presents a challenge for the drivers Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

"The various aerodynamic solutions they've had, we haven't found something that has broken the concept, whereas in the previous regulations there were a few things that actually did significantly compromise the concept.

"That mainly relates to the front wing endplates in the last generation car, the floor edges and all the furniture on the front wheel. All of those things made the wake characteristics significantly worse. We learned from that and I think hopefully there isn't any equivalent issue."

Aside from following other cars and the impact of dirty air, Tombazis also sees it as a positive that drivers still have their hands full with the new cars.

"They are still quite difficult cars to drive for the drivers, which I think is good, that they're not just cars that anybody can drive," he insisted. "Some of the aerodynamic regulations push towards teams not being able to address every single aspect of a car through a corner, and therefore they do have some challenges.

"I think when we have the 22 best drivers in the world, we should also have cars that are not exactly easy for my grandma to drive."

On top of that, the cars are slightly less physically demanding for the drivers than before, particularly because the ground-effect cars had to be run extremely low and stiff. "We have also raised the ride heights a bit, which means that they're not quite as brutal as last year," Tombazis added.

F1's ambition for 2031: cars another 80kg lighter

For the next set of regulations, the FIA would like the cars to be a further 80kg lighter, along with simpler power units Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

The overall package on the chassis side leaves Tombazis satisfied, although he stresses that the FIA wants to go further. That won’t be possible during the current cycle, but it is the target for the next set of regulations – which is due to come into force in 2031, or in 2030 if there is sufficient support.

"The cars are a bit lighter and a bit smaller, which the drivers have appreciated," Tombazis said. "Now, is that where I would like us to be? No. I would like us to be another 80 kilos lighter, and maybe still a bit shorter and a bit smaller in the future.

"That's the sort of target, that we do another big step from what was possible to do now. I think this is not a bad step, but it's not like I'm saying, 'Yes, job done, that's the target'. We want to go to another step of lightness in the future, and also the weight, a significant step."

For now, however, Tombazis is counting his blessings, particularly because the long-running trend of F1 cars becoming ever larger and heavier has finally been reversed.

"This is the first time I think Formula 1 cars have become lighter since probably the year 2000, I would say at least, or maybe earlier," he concluded.

Sports.title: Gasly vs Colapinto: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Alpine’s decision to fire Jack Doohan just six rounds into last season looked less brutal than it was only because Red Bull had axed Liam Lawson four rounds earlier.

Even so, come the end of the season it was debatable whether Doohan’s replacement Franco Colapinto had proved himself an obviously superior replacement, particularly considering he arrived at the team with more grand prix experience than poor Doohan had when he left.

However it was undoubtedly true that Alpine’s uncompetitive A525 was not a car to make a good first impression in. Pierre Gasly coaxed it into the points every now and then, something Colapinto never managed.

Now embarking on his first full season as a grand prix driver, Colapinto looks a much closer match for Gasly than he did last year. There is an interesting comparison to be drawn between Gasly and his former Alpine team mate Esteban Ocon: both have promising junior talents alongside them, but Oliver Bearman is posing more of a problem for Ocon than Colapinto is for Gasly.

That said, Colapinto has regularly followed along somewhere close behind Gasly, boosted Alpine’s points-scoring and accepted the ‘number two’ role when he’s had to. Colapinto was hard done by in Shanghai, when he finished 10th after being knocked into a spin by (ironically enough) Ocon.

When comparing their points haul it is also worth bearing in mind Gasly’s Monaco Grand Prix podium finish is subject to a challenge from rival teams over the post-race cancellation of his two pit lane speeding penalties. But even if Gasly keeps those points, Colapinto’s contribution to the team’s points score is very respectable. It’s hard to imaging the team wanting to replace him – unless a top-line driver seeking a car with a Mercedes power unit suddenly appears on the market.

Sports.title: Spotlight: How Monaco GP boss used sand trucks to beat Ecclestone | Brief
Sports.content:
As president of the Automobile Club de Monaco, Michel Boeri has been responsible for securing the future of Formula 1’s most famous race for over 50 years.

Before Liberty Media took over F1, that meant dealing with Bernie Ecclestone. In the seventies, Ecclestone ran the Formula One Constuctors’ Association, which negotiated on behalf of teams (a majority of which were British) with race promoters.

According to Boeri, Ecclestone’s uncompromising tactics required a firm response, as in one case soon after he took over as ACM president in 1972.

“Ecclestone was British, and he was a businessman. I was a rookie,” Boeri told Nice-Matin. “On the eve of the race, he told me: ‘Since we can’t agree on the fee, we’re going on strike.’

“There was no paddock yet, and the teams were based in the Portier parking lot. I called the Spada company and had the exits blocked with sand trucks. Then I went to Ecclestone and told him: ‘You don’t want to race? Fine. Then you’re not getting out.’ That got negotiations moving immediately.”

Boeri’s tactics achieved the desired result – though he also had the police ready to intervene.

“Ecclestone was a man of his word,” he said. “So I went down to the British camp to sign an agreement. There were no lawyers. It was simply: ‘I promise to move the trucks, and you promise to race. Signed, with love.’

“Being very brave, I had still called the police commander beforehand to tell him the British were drunk and aggressive, and to intervene if things got out of hand.

“I handed the paper to Ecclestone, he signed it, and I dropped to one knee. They took it the wrong way and thought a fight was about to break out. Then the cavalry charged! [laughs] It was ridiculous, but we weren’t writing a manual on diplomacy. You went on instinct. You felt your way through it.”

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Seven possible championship outcomes | Brief
Sports.content:
How is the championship fight most likely to turn out over the remaining races? Steve Rogers assesses the chances of each of the leading drivers.

I can see several different scenarios:

50% – The balance of performance is largely unchanged from the fist half of the season and Kimi wins (covers just holding on to domination).

20% – McLaren’s Zandvoort updates confirm them as the car to beat and Norris puts in a champion’s display to defend his title.

10% – Ferrari find a consistent window and become the car to beat but ‘Ferrari’ it away with mistakes and baffling strategies (Kimi wins)

8% – Ferrari find a consistent window and become the car to beat and Hamilton continues his first half form to win

2% – Ferrari find a consistent window and become the car to beat and and Leclerc finally finds consistency to back up his speed

5% – Kimi has a Piastri run of form and Russell gets out of his funk to win

5% – 2010-level of chaos and we go into the last race with several of the above still in it.

As I like an underdog, I went with Leclerc.

Sports.title: Lindblad vs Lawson: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Liam Lawson has finally begun what looks like being his first complete season with the same team and the stability appears to be paying off.

Having spent most of last season at Racing Bulls, Lawson has been a regular in the points. He has helped put the team fifth in the standings, on course for what would be its strongest championship finish in any of its guises.

But newcomer Arvid Lindblad has acquitted himself extremely well and goes into the summer break having tapped a strong vein of form. He’s scored in each of the last six grands prix and out-qualified Lawson in the last three – by decent margins, too.

So while Lawson’s numbers look good at the moment, he can’t be complacent about the growing threat on the other side of the Racing Bulls garage. Max Verstappen has all the reasons he needs to jump ship at the top team and if Lawson has a realistic chance of returning he needs to ensure he is the obvious choice. That won’t be the case as long as Lindblad keeps out-qualifying him.

As is often the case at Red Bull’s junior team, there is also pressure from below. Red Bull’s Nikola Tsolov leading the Formula 2 standings in his rookie campaign and the team will surely already be thinking about when he will be ready for a shot at F1.

Sports.title: Video: Honda explain Zandvoort ‘spec 2’ power unit changes | Brief
Sports.content:
Honda will introduce a ‘spec 2’ version of its RA626H power unit at the Dutch Grand Prix. The Japanese manufacturer is racing to catch up with its rivals after experiencing serious problems with vibration and insufficient power at the start of the sesason.

General trackside manager Shintaro Orihara said the new specification had hit their internal targets. “We focused to improve engine performance to make combustion faster,” he explained in a video released by Honda.

“We changed pre-chamber to make the combustion faster, and also we changed the piston shape also to get good combustion. Also, we modified some of the lubrication system to reduce friction. So we had a quite big risk to improve engine performance.”

Sports.title: Verstappen vs Hadjar: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar began his first full season at Red Bull knowing that the last driver in the same position as him lasted just two rounds before being booted out.

That must have been a daunting prospect to contemplate, though it bears pointing out that the senior race team management has changed significantly at Red Bull since Liam Lawson was shown the door after his pair of starts for the team last year.

The more experienced Yuki Tsunoda took Lawson’s place and became the latest in a series of drivers whose reputations took a brutal battering from occupying the garage adjacent to Max Verstappen’s. Tsunoda mustered just 7.2% of Red Bull’s points while alongside Verstappen.

This is the context in which to assess Hadjar’s performance this year. His 8-2 deficit in qualifying is nothing to brag about but he has been much closer to Verstappen over a single flying lap than his predecessors.

Hadjar has done vastly better at collecting points, too, claiming 38% of Red Bull’s score so far. True, compared to Tsunoda he’s had the benefit of a wider field spread between Red Bull and the midfield, but even so he’s already taken more than twice as many points as Tsunoda managed over his 22-race stint at the team last year.

He has achieved this alongside a formidable talent in a car which both drivers have termed “undriveable” on occasions. While the high level Verstappen operates at is so familiar it can almost be taken for granted (his superb second place in Hungary, for example), Hadjar has done a more than respectable job alongside him so far.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Has F1 failed to promote quality racing? | Brief
Sports.content:
Those in charge of Formula 1 have allowed its new rules to turn racing into a ‘battle of the bots’, says @RedPill:

I felt there was going to be some trust and proper direction within FIA and Liberty Media who owns the rights to F1 to make sure the quality of (human) racing was going to remain high quality. Boy, we were wrong. The whole debacle and agreed verbiage in contacts allowed the power unit manufacturers and investors to pretty much be the ones to dictate what was going to be allowed in F1, while retaining huge powers in the wording to prevent changes.

Fans, drivers, teams, FIA and Liberty Media are now stuck with it. I hate how the drivers are more passengers in their own cars while racing. Yes, there’s too much going in the cars, that the drivers can’t possibly manage everything and race in full anger, but this is no secret or anything new. The powers that be needed to craft specifications that used the latest tech, but still retain the drivers’ ability to fully race the car, the way a race car driver is suppose to race. That is why we watch the races.

We come and watch these F1 races because there’s humans in control of brilliant machinery, racing them to the ninth degree, but there’s a limit. If I wanted to watch automated machinery duke it out and see battle of bots I would instead go to robot contests, not F1.

Red Pill (@RedPill)

Sports.title: Top Rank’s Thin DAZN Schedule Tells Half The Story
Sports.content:
Darshan Desai of Uncrowned highlighted the unusual arrangement Wednesday while examining DAZN’s schedule. Raymond Muratalla fought Robson Conceição on a Golden Boy card earlier this month, Top Rank fighters Albert Gonzalez and Samuel Contreras competed on a Matchroom show in July, and Giovani Santillan takes another route when he faces Abass Baraou on September 11 in a ProBoxTV headliner.

Building a full show requires considerably more than placing a fighter on an existing lineup. Opponents require negotiation, purses need settling, and organizers must assemble a complete event around the roster. How costs are divided under Top Rank’s agreement with DAZN has not been made public.

Working alongside Golden Boy or Matchroom gives Top Rank flexible alternatives. Both outfits work extensively with DAZN, reducing the traditional network barriers that historically complicated cross-promotional deals.

Top Rank still has plenty of incentive to stage its own events when a leading fighter can anchor a marquee card. The proposed welterweight title bout between Devin Haney and Keyshawn Davis would have provided another major date before Davis declined the WBO process.

Whatever the reason for Top Rank’s limited number of DAZN dates so far, its fighters are finding work without waiting for the promoter to build an entire show around them.

Sports.title: WBC Threatens Noel Mikaelian’s Title Over Jai Opetaia Fight
Sports.content:
King and Benavidez promoter Sampson Lewkowicz reached an agreement for Mikaelian to defend his WBC cruiserweight title against Benavidez in December in Glendale, Arizona. Zuffa Boxing subsequently announced Mikaelian against Opetaia for September 12 in Las Vegas on the Ryan Garcia-Conor Benn card.

Mikaelian is already training for Opetaia, Pugmire reports, giving the WBC reason to seek an answer in the coming weeks on which fight he intends to take.

Benavidez may already have an alternate route. He teased an announcement Tuesday, and Pugmire reports his next bout will likely be against WBC interim cruiserweight champion Michal Cieslak for the title.

The promotional situation remains unusual. King and Lewkowicz had already struck their agreement when Zuffa announced Mikaelian as Opetaia’s opponent. Mikaelian then began preparing for the September fight despite remaining WBC champion, with Benavidez positioned as his mandatory challenger.

If Mikaelian proceeds with Opetaia, the WBC can remove him and leave Benavidez and Cieslak to fight for the championship. That would give Mikaelian the Zuffa fight he is training for, but without the WBC belt.

Sports.title: Hearn Targets Brandon Moore Next For Teremoana
Sports.content:
“I think we might fight him next, Brandon Moore,” Hearn said after the fight. “We have really got to find someone. It’s so frustrating in Australia because no one wants to fight him.”

A fight with Moore (19-1, 10 KOs) would provide an obvious measuring stick. He defeated Savage by a 10-round unanimous decision last September, dropping him in the seventh. His lone defeat came against Richard Torrez Jr., who knocked him out in five rounds in 2024.

Hearn felt Savage became frightened once he experienced Teremoana’s power.

“I was disappointed Savage didn’t get [further]. I don’t blame him, but it was just the fear. His eyes were popping out of his head as soon as he felt the power.”

Teremoana hardly pressed the accelerator in the opening round, throwing only a handful of punches before hurting Savage with a right hand late. Hearn liked the patience he showed rather than immediately going for the finish.

“I saw a guy that was a little bit more experienced tonight. Sort of took his time. I mean, he could have really done it in 30 seconds.”

Getting meaningful rounds has become increasingly difficult. Hearn conceded that fans will question the quality of Teremoana’s opposition and said Matchroom has reached the point where the competition must increase.

“There’ll be a lot of the public that will say, ‘Well, who’s he fighting?’ And I get that as well. We’ve got to step up,” Hearn said. “We do really, really need rounds.”

Hearn wants Teremoana to fight twice more this year and believes another four or five bouts are needed before he challenges for a world heavyweight title. His target is the back end of 2027, when Teremoana will be 29.

“He needs someone that can take him five or six rounds,” Hearn said. “Sooner or later there’s going to be a 10-round, 12-round war in there, and he’ll be ready.”

Anthony Joshua has also taken notice of Teremoana.

“AJ said to me a few times, ‘What’s this Teremoana?’ I’m like, ‘He’s a fucking monster.’”

Hearn expects a different type of fight once Teremoana encounters heavyweights willing and capable of attacking him rather than simply trying to survive.

Sports.title: Teremoana Teremoana Crushes DeAndre Savage in Two
Sports.content:
Teremoana dictated the opening round, forcing Savage onto the defensive while patiently looking for an opening.

In the co-main event, Michael “Pretty Boy” Zerafa stopped Alejandro “El Venado” Ortiz after nine rounds of their scheduled 10-round middleweight bout.

Zerafa established his jab over the opening two rounds before Ortiz found more success in the third, landing several left hooks to the chin. Zerafa countered effectively and produced a strong fourth round.

Ortiz landed a hard right hand midway through the fifth, but Zerafa regained control in the sixth by increasing his output. The Australian broke through in the ninth, hurting Ortiz and overwhelming him with punches. Ortiz struggled back to his corner after the bell, and his team stopped the fight before the 10th round.

Jasmine Parr defeated Jemma Peart by unanimous decision over eight two-minute rounds in their flyweight bout.

Parr controlled much of the opening three rounds by outlanding Peart, who had greater success with her jab in the fourth. Parr occasionally switched to southpaw in the fifth and sixth while maintaining the higher work rate.

The seventh was the most competitive round before Parr closed strongly in the eighth. All three judges scored the bout 80-72.

At super middleweight, Jack Bowen stopped Dalielibieke at 2:15 of the seventh round.

Bowen used an effective jab early and rocked Dalielibieke with an uppercut in the second. Both connected with hard right hands late in the third before the exchanges became heavier in the fourth.

Another right uppercut from Bowen hurt Dalielibieke midway through the fifth. Dalielibieke responded with one of his better rounds in the sixth, but Bowen regained control in the seventh. A sustained combination prompted referee Paul Tapley to stop the contest.

Lekaysha Woodbridge defeated Sothia Sitthichai over five two-minute rounds in their flyweight bout. Referee Paul Tapley scored the fight 50-45 for Woodbridge.

Light heavyweight Omar El-Abdallah stopped Jordan Towns after three rounds of their scheduled five-round bout. The two were competitive through the opening three rounds, but Towns was unable to answer the bell for the fourth.

In welterweight action, Reube Thornberry stopped Lachlan Harrington at 1:40 of the second round of their scheduled four-round bout.

Sports.title: Jake Paul’s MVP Signs IBF Champion Elif Turhan
Sports.content:
Turhan gives Jake Paul’s promotion another major piece at 135 pounds. Caroline Dubois holds the WBC and WBO championships, while Stephanie Han owns the WBA belt.

That leaves MVP working with fighters who control all four major lightweight titles.

Turhan punched her way into that company last December in Monte Carlo. She broke down Brazilian Olympic gold medalist Beatriz Ferreira and forced a fifth-round stoppage to seize the IBF crown, registering the defining victory of her professional career.

She has since strengthened her position with wins over Taylah Gentzen in January and Gabriella Tellez in June.

Turhan brings pressure and finishing instinct to a division loaded with potential championship fights. She likes to close the distance, force exchanges and punish opponents once her combinations begin finding the target.

The Istanbul fighter becomes the first Turkish boxer to join MVP and follows Nicolson as the second addition produced by the promotion’s agreement with Matchroom.

Turhan believes the partnership can push her toward more championship opportunities.

“I am incredibly excited to be part of this powerful collaboration. This marks a major signal of the exciting initiatives we will undertake for women’s boxing globally, and I am deeply honored to be involved in this journey with all my strength and energy.”

Her next opponent has yet to be confirmed, but her ambitions reach beyond defending the IBF belt.

“I am excited for the opportunities that will come my way as I look to win more major World Titles.”

That pursuit creates an obvious pressure point at lightweight. Dubois controls two belts, Han holds another and Turhan carries the IBF championship.

If MVP eventually matches its lightweight champions, Turhan will have to establish her pressure against fighters capable of controlling distance, countering her entries and punishing her on the way inside.

Sports.title: Teremoana vs. DeAndre Savage Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Teremoana Teremoana improved to 12-0 with a second-round knockout of DeAndre Savage after another destructive heavyweight finish. Savage survived the opening round despite absorbing several heavy shots as Teremoana began finding his distance and opening up. That resistance ended quickly in the second. Teremoana cracked Savage with a big punch that buckled the American’s legs but left him standing. The Australian kept hunting the finish, dropped Savage moments later, and watched as he failed to beat the referee’s count. Savage became only the third opponent to take Teremoana beyond the opening round, but the extra three minutes merely delayed another knockout for the Australian heavyweight.

Michael Zerafa broke down Alejandro Ortiz for a stoppage victory on the Gold Coast after taking command in the later rounds. Zerafa began forcing Ortiz onto the back foot, then cracked him with a heavy shot in the seventh as the pressure increased. His corner demanded he keep letting his hands go while staying smart, telling him Ortiz was hurt whenever he opened up. Zerafa responded by pressing harder and keeping Ortiz under fire. The breakthrough came when Zerafa dropped Ortiz and immediately looked to close the show. Ortiz climbed off the canvas but remained hurt, and the fight was stopped soon afterward when he had taken enough. The victory gave Zerafa the result he needed after entering the fight under pressure and facing questions over his recent form.

Sports.title: Jack Dempsey’s Harry Wills Problem Never Went Away
Sports.content:
Following Jack Johnson’s 1910 victory over Jim Jeffries, racial violence erupted across the United States. The possibility of another Black heavyweight challenging a white champion encountered resistance from promoters, regulators, and others concerned about another interracial title fight.

Wills paid heavily for that environment.

A Dempsey-Wills fight nearly materialized in 1922 when promoter Tex Rickard selected a date and had tickets printed for a proposed bout in New Jersey. The promotion collapsed when the financing needed to meet Dempsey’s guarantee failed.

Another attempt ran into opposition in New York, where athletic commission chairman William Muldoon resisted an interracial heavyweight championship fight over concerns about racial unrest.

Dempsey also gave his critics ammunition. He drew the color line early in his championship reign before later changing his public position. His long stretches of inactivity intensified criticism that Wills was being denied an opportunity he had earned. Yet Wills himself resisted blaming Dempsey.

“My only regret in life is that I never got a shot at Dempsey, [and] I’m sure I could have beaten him,” Wills later said. “It wasn’t Jack’s fault. He wasn’t scared of anyone. He was a great fighter.”

Dempsey lost the heavyweight championship to Gene Tunney in 1926. Wills never fought for the world title.

The missing fight should count when Dempsey’s championship reign is evaluated. Wills was precisely the type of challenger a champion needed to defeat to remove questions about his dominance.

Placing the entire responsibility on Dempsey, however, ignores the racial barriers, regulators, promoters and failed financing that repeatedly interfered with the fight.

More than a century later, nobody knows what would have happened if Jack Dempsey and Harry Wills had finally met. That unanswered question is why Wills remains an unavoidable part of Dempsey’s legacy.

Sports.title: Teofimo Sr. Dismisses Shakur Stevenson’s Vacant-Belt Championships
Sports.content:
“This fight is about Teofimo Lopez trying to get the world title again, become a real three-division world champion. No vacant belts,” Lopez Sr. said to Fighthype. “Shakur got like two vacant belts, right? So, to me, he’s not a real three-division world champion. My son is going to do it the right way. We’re going to go straight to the champion. No vacant belt.”

Stevenson has actually won world titles across four divisions. His first came against Joet Gonzalez for the vacant WBO featherweight belt in 2019. He then stopped reigning WBO junior lightweight champion Jamel Herring in 2021 before defeating Edwin De Los Santos for the vacant WBC lightweight title in November 2023.

The fourth belt is difficult for Lopez Sr. to dismiss under his own standard. Shakur took the WBO light welterweight title from Teofimo in January, giving him two divisional championships won by defeating reigning titleholders.

Lopez Sr. also criticized Shakur’s fighting style and questioned how much further Stevenson can climb through the weight classes.

“I would love to fight him again. Let’s hope that we can get him before we move up too high,” Lopez Sr. said. “I don’t think Shakur can go up in the weight divisions. He’s too chinny. He doesn’t like to get hit. He’s a boring fighter.”

He believes Teofimo fought the wrong fight against Shakur. In his view, Teofimo should have boxed from the back foot instead of following the southpaw to his right all night.

Ghana News.title: Volta Regional House of Chiefs congratulates Ablakwa, pledges stronger ties with Foreign Affairs Ministry
Ghana News.content:
The Volta Regional House of Chiefs has paid a courtesy call on the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, to congratulate him on his appointment and birthday and strengthen ties between the traditional leadership of the region and the Ministry.

The delegation, led by the President of the Volta Regional House of Chiefs and Paramount Chief of the Anfoega Traditional Area, Togbe Tepre Hodo IV, visited the Minister at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Accra on Wednesday, August 12, 2026.

Togbe Tepre Hodo IV said the visit was also an opportunity to deepen the relationship between the House and the Ministry as they work towards the development of the Volta Region and Ghana.

Mr Ablakwa expressed appreciation to the chiefs for the visit and their congratulatory messages.

He said he was particularly grateful that the traditional leaders had travelled to Accra to meet him, noting that he had initially intended to visit the House of Chiefs himself, but the offer was respectfully declined.

The Minister described the visit as a privilege and welcomed the opportunity to host the traditional leaders at his official workplace.

Togbe Tepre Hodo IV commended Mr Ablakwa for what he described as his dedicated service to Ghana and his efforts to promote development in his constituency and the Volta Region.

He noted that the region had, over the years, faced challenges in accessing its fair share of national resources and development opportunities.

According to him, there have been significant changes in recent times, which he attributed partly to the Minister’s efforts to ensure that the interests of the Volta Region receive greater attention.

The President of the Volta Regional House of Chiefs also praised Mr Ablakwa for maintaining a strong connection with the region despite his national responsibilities.

He encouraged the Minister to continue championing the interests of the Volta Region while advancing Ghana’s broader national interests.

Ghana News.title: Baba Yara stadium will be ready for 2026/27 football season – NSA boss
Ghana News.content:
Director General of the National Sports Authority (NSA), Yaw Ampofo Ankrah says the Baba Yara Stadium will be ready for the first game of the 2026/27 Ghana football season.

The NSA boss toured the stadium together with the board chairman of NSA, Dr Fred Awaah and NSA estate boss Mr. Ebo.

The 2026/27 Ghana Premier League season will officially get underway over the weekend of September 4–7, 2026.

After inspecting the stadium, he commended the Ashanti Regional Directorate for its effort in restoring the stadium to its functionality.

The Director General assessed the progress of pitch condition and also inspected the stability of the scoreboard and floodlights.

Speaking to the media, Yaw Ampofo expressed confidence the facility will be ready in time for next football season.

“The pitch is responding to treatment and the rehabilitation is on course. I believe in a few weeks it should be in good, stead, strong enough, robust to host football matches including the Ghana Premier League and any other international match in the need arises,” he said.

The NSA was criticized heavily after video of groundkeepers using hoes on the pitch instead of modern turf maintenance equipment went viral.

Yaw Ampofo backs the move of the regional directorate: “We don’t have the tools that are common, we will acquire them soon but I commend them [Ashanti Regional Directorate] for tackling the weeds from its source.

"In the past when the sprinklers were not working, they resorted to the Fire Service and other means to ensure the grass doesn’t die. Perhaps people didn’t understand the images but now they do”.

With Ghana’s 2027 AFCON qualifiers set to start in September, there are speculation about hosting home games at the Baba Yara Stadium in Kumasi.

But Yaw Ampofo believes the decision to host Black Stars lies with the sports ministry and GFA after consulting the engineers in charge of the facility.

Despite the improvement in work done at the stadium, there are more than three thousand seats to be repaired after violence during school sports competitions in January destroyed some of the seats.

The NSA boss reiterated that the Ghana Education Service has agreed to fund the restoration project.

Ghana News.title: Speak law, not emotions – Amaliba fires back at Mercer on Sedina Tamakloe’s release
Ghana News.content:
Former Director of Legal Affairs of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), Abraham Amaliba, has rejected claims by a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Andrews Agyapa Mercer, that the release of former Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC) Chief Executive Officer, Sedina Christine Tamakloe-Attionu, vindicates the opposition party’s concerns about selective justice.

Mr Amaliba said Ms Tamakloe-Attionu’s release was the logical consequence of her acquittal and discharge by the Court of Appeal.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Wednesday, August 12, he argued that the government could not have prevented her release after an independent court had delivered its judgment.

“How can a decision of a court of competent jurisdiction become a matter of ‘we told you so’? It cannot ... I think that we should speak law and stop speaking with emotions,” he said.

Mr Amaliba stressed that the judiciary is an independent arm of government and that its decisions must be respected.

He said even if the NDC government had wanted Ms Tamakloe-Attionu to remain in custody, it could not have simply overturned or ignored the court’s decision.

“Even if we as a party wanted to do it, how could we have done it? Another arm of government, independent as it is, and respectable as it is, gave that ruling,” he added.

His comments followed remarks by lawyer and NPP member Andrews Agyapa Mercer, who said he was not surprised by Ms Tamakloe-Attionu’s release.

Mr Mercer argued that the development reinforced concerns that the government was selectively pursuing cases involving political opponents.

“I really am not surprised. The script that was formulated when the NDC came into office commenced with the nolle prosequi that they entered for all persons affiliated with the NDC who were standing trial in the courts,” he said.

Mr Mercer further questioned the circumstances surrounding the Attorney-General’s decision to withdraw the application for a stay of execution after the Court of Appeal acquitted and discharged Ms Tamakloe-Attionu.

He suggested that the development vindicated earlier concerns raised by the NPP about the government’s handling of cases involving individuals associated with political parties.

Mr Amaliba, however, maintained that such claims failed to account for the role of the judiciary in the matter.

He said the appropriate approach was to examine the legal basis for the court’s decision rather than interpret the outcome through a political lens.

Ghana News.title: NSA releases 121,754 PIN codes for 2026/2027 National Service Year
Ghana News.content:
The National Service Authority (NSA) has released PIN codes for 121,754 prospective national service personnel for the 2026/2027 National Service Year.

The release marks the opening of the registration process for eligible graduates required to undertake national service under the National Service Authority Act, 2024 (Act 1119).

Online registration began on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, and will close on Wednesday, August 26.

The Authority has urged all eligible prospective personnel to complete their registration within the stipulated period to avoid delays in deployment.

The NSA said tertiary institutions submitted a total of 144,023 prospective personnel for consideration.

Of that number, 122,712 were approved, with records created for 121,754 unique persons.

However, 958 approved submissions have not been promoted pending further verification, while another 21,311 submissions were rejected pending further identity verification.

The Authority said the 121,754 PIN codes released represent applicants whose submissions successfully passed the requisite validation and verification processes.

The remaining 22,269 submissions have been withheld pending the outcome of further checks.

Prospective personnel with PIN codes are required to access the NSA's registration portal, activate their PIN codes and complete the online enrolment process.

A registration fee is also required to activate the PIN code before applicants can access the enrolment platform. Payment is to be made via Mobile Money across all networks.

The NSA said it has introduced enhanced security measures to strengthen the integrity of the registration process and prevent fraudulent enrolments.

These include facial biometric verification against Ghana Card records held by the National Identification Authority (NIA).

Applicants must also provide a valid GhanaPost GPS address, which the Authority says will support accurate deployment and proximity-based postings.

Real-time verification mechanisms have also been integrated into the registration platform to improve data accuracy.

The NSA has further reminded tertiary institutions whose accreditation status remains unresolved to engage the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) to regularise their status.

The Authority said it would continue processing eligible graduates from such institutions once GTEC confirms their accreditation.

Prospective personnel requiring assistance have been directed to use the support channels provided on the NSA registration portal.

Ghana News.title: NSA withholds 22,269 national service PIN codes over identity verification issues
Ghana News.content:
The National Service Authority (NSA) has withheld PIN codes for 22,269 prospective national service personnel over unresolved identity verification issues.

The affected graduates are among 144,023 personnel submitted by tertiary institutions for the 2026/2027 National Service Year.

According to figures released by the Authority on Wednesday, August 12, 21,311 submissions were rejected pending further identity verification, while another 958 were approved but not promoted as they await additional verification.

The development comes as online registration for prospective service personnel officially opens.

The NSA said 122,712 of the 144,023 submissions were approved.

However, only 121,754 unique persons have so far had their records created and PIN codes released.

The Authority explained that these are prospective service personnel whose submissions successfully passed the required validation and verification processes.

The remaining submissions have been withheld pending the outcome of further checks.

The NSA said it undertook rigorous validation and verification in collaboration with relevant regulatory institutions to ensure that only eligible graduates from accredited tertiary institutions are mobilised.

According to the Authority, the measures are intended to protect the integrity of the national service enrolment process and eliminate duplicate, inflated and irregular submissions.

It has also reminded tertiary institutions whose accreditation status remains unresolved to engage the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) to regularise their status.

The NSA said eligible graduates from such institutions could subsequently be processed once GTEC confirms their accreditation.

For the 121,754 prospective service personnel whose PIN codes have been released, online registration began on Wednesday, August 12, and will close on Wednesday, August 26, 2026.

The Authority has urged eligible personnel to complete the process within the stipulated period to avoid delays in deployment.

The NSA is also using enhanced verification measures, including facial biometric checks against Ghana Card records, GhanaPost GPS address validation and real-time verification mechanisms integrated into the registration platform.

The 22,269 prospective personnel whose PIN codes have been withheld will have to await the outcome of the verification process before they can access the registration platform.

The NSA has not indicated when the outstanding verification process will be completed.

Ghana News.title: Eyipe’s sanitation crisis raises concerns over public health and coastal pollution
Ghana News.content:
Residents of Eyipe, a community in Winneba in the Central Region, are raising concerns over persistent sanitation challenges, including improper waste disposal, open defecation and the poor management of wastewater.

The situation has become particularly worrying because of the community’s proximity to the sea. Rubbish can be found in parts of the community, especially around the shoreline, while wastewater from households is sometimes discharged into open areas where waste has already accumulated.

For residents, the problem goes beyond the appearance of their surroundings. They are concerned about the possible effects on public health and the coastal environment.

Waste disposal remains a challenge

Some residents say the cost of waste collection contributes to improper waste disposal in the community.

According to them, some households struggle to pay the waste levy regularly and resort to disposing of rubbish in open spaces, sometimes early in the morning.

Residents also expressed concerns about wastewater from washing and other household activities being discharged into open areas. In some locations, the wastewater mixes with accumulated rubbish, creating unhygienic conditions.

The situation is more concerning around the shoreline, where some residents say rubbish is dumped close to the sea.

With the community located near the coast, residents fear that continued dumping could contribute to marine pollution and affect the environment and people who depend on the sea.

Residents express frustration

Some residents said they had reported the sanitation problem several times but had seen limited improvement.

Others declined to speak about the issue, explaining that they had raised similar concerns in the past without seeing enough action.

For these residents, the problem has therefore become more than the presence of rubbish. It has also created a sense of frustration over whether their concerns are receiving adequate attention.

Assembly acknowledges sanitation problem

The Assembly Member for the area, Hon. Kofi Kumi, acknowledged that sanitation remains a challenge in Eyipe.

He said the community does not have enough dustbins to provide residents with adequate facilities for proper waste disposal.

He also identified the absence of Zoomlion waste collection services as another challenge, saying the lack of regular collection makes it difficult to manage waste generated by households.

Despite these challenges, he said community clean-up exercises are organised regularly and residents are encouraged to participate.

However, residents say the clean-up exercises provide only temporary relief because the community continues to face difficulties with regular waste collection and disposal.

Public health concerns

The sanitation situation has also raised concerns about the health of residents.

A sanitation officer who spoke about the situation presented records of cholera and diarrhoea cases and explained the health risks associated with poor sanitation.

Improper waste disposal and open defecation can create conditions that increase the spread of disease. For residents living near areas where rubbish accumulates, sanitation is therefore a public health issue as much as an environmental one.

Concerns over coastal pollution

Eyipe’s proximity to the sea adds another dimension to the sanitation challenge.

Waste dumped near the shoreline and wastewater discharged carelessly can eventually enter the marine environment, raising concerns about coastal pollution and its potential impact on marine life.

The situation also threatens the cleanliness of an environment that supports the livelihoods and daily activities of people in the community.

Calls for a lasting solution

The sanitation challenges in Eyipe are linked to several factors, including improper waste disposal, the cost of waste collection, inadequate disposal facilities and limited regular waste collection services.

Addressing the situation will therefore require more than periodic clean-up exercises.

Residents need access to adequate waste bins, reliable waste collection services and affordable disposal options. Continuous public education could also encourage households to adopt safer waste disposal practices.

The concerns about open defecation further highlight the need for access to suitable toilet facilities and sustained sanitation education.

For residents, the ultimate goal is not simply to have a clean community immediately after a clean-up exercise. They want a system that keeps the community clean throughout the year.

As Eyipe continues to confront its sanitation challenges, the issue has become a reminder that public health and environmental protection are closely connected.

For a community located beside the sea, addressing poor sanitation is not only about improving the appearance of the community. It is about protecting residents, preserving the coastline and ensuring a healthier environment for future generations.

By Daniella Adoma Sarpong

Ghana News.title: My studio caught fire after I ignored God’s warning to ditch secular music – Perez Musik
Ghana News.content:
Gospel musician Perez Musik

Gospel musician Perez Musik has recounted how a fire that destroyed his recording studio became a turning point in his decision to leave secular music and focus on his Christian faith.

Speaking on The Career Trail on Joy Learning TV and Joy News, Perez Musik said he had received what he described as several prophetic warnings to turn away from secular music, but continued recording artistes at his studio.

“I had been getting prophecies that you need to start doing the work of God and I've been stubborn. Because I was enjoying the secular, recording the boys in the area. Article Wan and all. They used to come to my studio to record,” he recalled.

He said the studio was later destroyed by fire after he had invested money in new equipment.

Perez Musik recalled receiving money for his work as a sound engineer on Anita Erskine's Fashion 101. He decided to use part of the money to upgrade his studio.

According to him, he had an uneasy feeling before purchasing the equipment but proceeded with the purchase.

“Just when I stepped into the shop, I heard a voice. ‘So these equipment that you're going to buy, if it catches fire and everything gets burned, what will you do?’ But I still went ahead and bought the equipment,” he said.

He said the studio caught fire on 24 December.

“I woke up in the morning, everything was fine. I was just going to pick something. I came back, the studio was on fire,” he recalled.

Although the incident was painful, Perez Musik said he came to regard it as a turning point in his life.

“It realigned my thinking. It changed my perspective on life. That, you know, material things are not things that you can hold on to. There's something higher. There's something greater. There's something more, which is Christ,” he said.

He subsequently became more involved in church activities, prayer and Bible study. He also said he quit drinking and smoking as he took his Christian faith more seriously.

Perez Musik said he had long believed he possessed a prophetic gift but had resisted the responsibility he associated with it.

“I knew the gift was there. It's just that I was shying away from the responsibility and the requirement that comes with the gift,” he said.

His spiritual transformation eventually influenced his music.

“Then I started doing the urban gospel. My first album, Tenacity, was an urban gospel. So that was when everything started. From there it's been one song after the other,” he said.

He also explained how he adopted the name Perez, drawing inspiration from the biblical account of Tamar and Judah in Genesis.

Perez said the name represented breakthrough and reflected what he regarded as his transition from his previous lifestyle into a new one centred on his faith.

Ghana News.title: The trouble with being online all the time
Ghana News.content:
The growing amount of time people spend on smartphones and social media is raising concerns about its impact on attention, relationships and everyday life, particularly among young people.

For many, checking a phone has become part of almost every daily activity. People scroll through social media while eating, wait for messages while studying and turn to their phones whenever they have a few moments of free time.

What may appear to be a harmless habit can gradually become difficult to control.

Psychologists and digital-wellbeing experts have increasingly warned that excessive screen use can affect people's ability to concentrate and remain present in their daily lives. Constant notifications and the pressure to respond can also make it difficult for people to disconnect.

Social media adds another dimension to the problem. Platforms are designed to keep users engaged by constantly providing new content. Users can spend hours viewing carefully selected images and videos showing other people's achievements, holidays and lifestyles.

This can encourage unhealthy comparisons, particularly when people compare their everyday lives with the carefully edited versions of other people's lives presented online.

The issue is not that technology itself is harmful. Smartphones and the internet have transformed communication, education, business and access to information. The challenge is finding a healthy balance between digital activity and real-world interaction.

For some people, that balance begins with simple changes.

Putting phones away during meals, turning off unnecessary notifications and taking regular breaks from social media can create opportunities for people to focus on their surroundings and interact with others without digital distractions.

Taking a walk without constantly checking a phone can also provide an opportunity to think, observe and enjoy the environment.

There is also growing recognition that boredom is not necessarily a bad thing. Having periods without constant entertainment can give people time to reflect, develop ideas and engage in activities that require creativity.

For young people especially, developing healthy digital habits may be important as smartphones and social media become increasingly integrated into education, work and social life.

The solution, therefore, may not be to abandon technology but to use it more deliberately.

The internet is unlikely to disappear, and social media will remain an important part of modern communication. However, individuals can decide how much control these platforms have over their time and attention.

The challenge is to remain connected without becoming so connected that the real world is forgotten.

Sometimes, putting the phone down may be the first step towards noticing what has been happening around us all along.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
