World.title: Artistic research project on gardens and communities in Romania, Hungary on view in Debrecen
World.content:
Cultivators of Life: Growing Seedbeds of Knowledge, an artistic research and production program carried out by tranzit.ro/Bucharest in partnership with the Centre for Modern and Contemporary Arts in Debrecen (MODEM), will be on view at MODEM starting September 5.

The project brings together artists, researchers and practitioners in an exhibition “that explores the garden as a space for producing and transmitting knowledge.” It began with gardens and communities around Bucharest and developed through artist residencies, international exchanges, workshops and field research.

Curated by Adelina Luft and Krisztián Gábor Török, the exhibition involved artists, researchers, gardeners and community practitioners from Europe, the Caribbean, Latin America and Southeast Asia to explore cultivation not only as an agricultural activity, but also as a form of knowledge production, community building and imagining ecological futures, a presentation of the exhibition reads.

At the heart of the project are six gardens in Romania and Hungary, including the Cosmos Garden at the Experimental Research Station for Art and Life in Siliștea Snagovului, the Seed House Garden, the Uzura Garden, Studio-Garden Crețești, and two gardens in Debrecen. “Over the course of two years, these became spaces for artistic research, encounters and knowledge exchange, while the experiences and practices of the people who care for them entered into dialogue with contemporary art, ecology, science and local forms of knowledge.”

The exhibition features works and research by artists including Alex Bodea, Annalee Davis, Aterraterra, Colectivo Suumil Móokt’aan, Fuzzy Earth, Harun Morrison, Horia Bernea, Kitti Gosztola & Bence Pálinkás, Marina Sulima, Martin Piaček, Mónica de Miranda, de Onkruidenier Collective, Orsolya Gál, PARI feat. Anang Saptoto and Raluca Popa, alongside artistic documentation of the gardens by Irina Bobei, Maria Doni and Gabriela Cozma.

The exhibition will be on view until November 8.

(Photo: Martin Piaček Frutteto. Il breve archivio del dono/ Orchard. A Brief Archive of the Gift; curated by Lýdia Pribišová)

World.title: Bucharest connected to Beijing through direct flights starting in September
World.content:
Romanians will be able to travel directly to the People’s Republic of China starting on September 4, after the official inauguration of the air route between Beijing and Bucharest, operated by Air China, according to an official press release published on Tuesday, August 11.

The new round-trip air route operated by Air China, connecting Beijing (PEK) - Bucharest (OTP) - Zagreb (ZAG), marks a new stage in the development of connectivity and cooperation between the two countries, said the Embassy of Romania in the People’s Republic of China.

According to the same source, the resumption of direct flights reflects the common commitment and good cooperation in promoting and facilitating bilateral contacts, especially in areas such as tourism, economic cooperation, cultural and people-to-people exchanges.

The flights will be operated weekly, on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

“The resumption of direct flights between Bucharest and Beijing represents a major diplomatic and economic success, intended to bring our communities closer together. This connectivity corridor will stimulate and open new opportunities for dialogue and cooperation, generating concrete advantages on multiple levels of common interest,” said Romania’s ambassador to the People’s Republic of China, Dan-Horia Maxim, quoted by Agerpres.

The official inauguration ceremony of the new Beijing - Bucharest - Zagreb route, hosted by the Embassy of Romania in Beijing, in partnership with the Embassy of Croatia and Air China, brought together officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People’s Republic of China, other institutions and specialized agencies, such as the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC), representatives of local and international news agencies and media groups, the business community and the tourism sector.

Romania was also connected to China before. In 1974, TAROM launched a flight for the first time on the Bucharest - Beijing route.

World.title: Cushman & Wakefield Echinox: Net take-up generated 73% of Bucharest’s office demand in H1
World.content:
Bucharest's office market is seeing a recovery in occupier demand driven by new lease transactions and expansions, against a backdrop of limited new supply. Net take-up accounted for 73% of the total leasing activity in H1 2026, up from 53% during the same period of 2025, according to the Cushman & Wakefield Echinox Marketbeat Office Q2 2026 report.

At the same time, the citywide vacancy rate continued its downward trend to 11.6%, the lowest level since Q3 2020. This trend was primarily supported by stronger demand from companies operating in the IT&C sector.

The total office take-up in Bucharest reached 109,500 sqm during the first six months of the year, of which 60,400 sqm were leased in the second quarter alone. Although the overall leasing activity remained approximately 10% below the level recorded in H1 2025, the structure of demand points to a rebound in transactions with a positive net impact on office occupancy levels.

The IT&C sector regained its position as the largest occupier segment in the capital city, leasing more than 30,500 sqm in H1 2026, nearly double the volume registered during the same period last year. By contrast, the financial sector, which led leasing activity in 2025, recorded a significant decline in transaction volumes.

Among the most notable office transactions completed during the second quarter were Rohde & Schwarz Topex's 9,600 sqm renewal and expansion in IRIDE Business Park 19 (Dimitrie Pompeiu), Veolia’s pre-lease of 6,000 sqm in Green Court D (Floreasca-Barbu Vacarescu), Strabag's pre-lease of 4,600 sqm in Queens District (Floreasca-Barbu Vacarescu), as well as Evoke’s renewal of 2,400 sqm in Bucharest Business Garden (Center-West).

On the supply side, the market continues to be defined by a lack of new deliveries. No office projects were completed during the first half of the year, keeping Bucharest's modern office stock stable at approximately 3.43 million sqm.

Approximately 216,000 sqm are currently under construction and scheduled for delivery in phases through early 2028. Given this development timeline, the shortage of high-quality office spaces is expected to persist in the short and medium terms, maintaining upward pressure on prime rents across the city.

The five largest office projects currently under construction are the second phase of Timpuri Noi Square (Center, 60,000 sqm, developed by Vastint), ARC Project (Center-West, 30,000 sqm, developed by PPF Real Estate), AFI Central Tower (Center, 28,000 sqm, AFI Europe), Queens District (Floreasca-Barbu Vacarescu, 23,000 sqm, Speedwell) and One Technology District (Dimitrie Pompeiu, 20,600 sqm, One United Properties).

The prime headline rents remained stable in Q2, with levels between EUR 21.00 - 22.00/ sqm/ month being the norm in non-boutique projects in CBD (a series of high-profile buildings have asking rents of up to EUR 25.00 - 26.00).

From a regional perspective, Bucharest remains one of the most competitive office markets in Central and Eastern Europe. Its rental benchmarks are broadly comparable to those in Bratislava and remain below levels recorded in Warsaw and Prague. Across the CEE region, prime office rents increased by approximately 5% year-on-year, outperforming the European average of 4.5%.

World.title: Romanians among least wanted immigrants in United Kingdom, YouGov survey says
World.content:
Romanians are among the least wanted immigrants in the United Kingdom, according to a YouGov survey published on Monday, August 10.

Roughly 47% of respondents in the survey said that they would like to see fewer immigrants from Romania, down from 51% in 2016. Still, the figure placed Romanians in fifth place, tied with immigrants from Israel. The top places were taken by Russians (58%), Pakistanis (52%) and Nigerians (48%).

Around 18% of the Britons who took part in the public survey said that no immigrants from Romania should be accepted.

Overall, Romanians were in sixth place in the ranking of the “unwanted,” tied with immigrants from Egypt. Ahead of them were again Russians, Pakistanis, Israelis and Nigerians.

The survey also showed that 29% of those questioned believe that Romanians should be admitted, but in smaller numbers than at present. In this respect, Romanians fared the worst and shared the top position in the ranking with immigrants from India.

On the other side, 25% of Britons said that the current number of Romanian immigrants can be maintained, while 7% said that the number can be increased.

By comparison, attitudes towards migrants from Poland have improved substantially since 2016, with most Britons (53%) now either happy with current numbers or wanting more to come.

According to the survey, the immigrants viewed most favorably by the British were the Irish, Canadians, Australians, Swedes, Germans and Japanese. Immigrants from countries such as South Africa, Mexico, Thailand and China were also viewed more favorably than Romanians.

The survey also revealed that around 43% of the British believe immigration has been mostly bad for the country, up from 33% in 2016. Another 29% said it has been both good and bad, and 21% claimed it has been mostly good.

World.title: Two drifting drones destroyed near Romania’s Neptun Deep exploitation area
World.content:
Two Gerbera-type drones were destroyed on Tuesday, August 11, by divers of the Romanian Army in the exclusive economic zone, approximately 90 nautical miles (around 165 kilometers) from Constanța, in the Neptun Deep exploitation area, according to interim defence minister Radu Miruță.

The drones were observed around 8 AM by one of the vessels carrying out works in the Neptun Deep platform area, and a Coast Guard vessel with military personnel on board moved to the area.

“Two drifting UAV systems and several other pieces of debris were identified. The Defense Ministry contacted the Ukrainian partners, who confirmed that the systems do not belong to them,” the minister also stated.

For the safety of the navigation route and the works being carried out around the platform, the authorities decided to destroy the drones. The two UAVs were neutralized through controlled detonation, while a drone fragment, which did not present a pyrotechnic risk, was taken on board.

According to Digi24, Gerbera drones are multifunctional unmanned aerial vehicles designed as a much cheaper and simplified version of the Iranian Shahed-136 drones. They are used by the Russian army mainly as decoys to saturate and mislead air defense systems, but also for reconnaissance or attack missions. They fly alongside Shahed attack drones to force defense systems to consume expensive missiles on false targets.

Gerbera drones are capable of identifying the positions of radars and active anti-aircraft batteries while these are trying to shoot them down, and they can also function as signal amplifiers to extend the range and control of other drones in the network.

The drones can also be equipped with a small explosive payload (approximately 6-8 kg), but this role is secondary because of their reduced autonomy when carrying heavier loads.

World.title: Romanian artisanal dessert brand Franțuzisme launches after EUR 66,000 investment
World.content:
Franțuzisme, a Romanian artisanal dessert brand founded by Cătălina Clément, is launching following a EUR 66,000 investment made through the Bucharest-Ilfov Regional Program 2021–2027.

The investment covered the fit-out of the pastry workshop, the acquisition of professional equipment and the development of the brand. The project functions as a social enterprise.

The founder trained in contemporary dessert artistry with pastry chef Cédric Grolet and the pastry workshop translates the techniques of contemporary French pastry “into its own approach centered on taste, texture and aesthetics.”

“Franțuzisme did not start with a business idea. It started with a question that science does not take into consideration: what do children miss when they grow up without experiencing the authentic taste of a fruit? In looking for the answer and trying to give my daughter that experience, I came to study contemporary dessert artistry with Cédric Grolet and to build a brand that places the experience of the dessert, rather than simply the product itself, at the heart of every creation,” Cătălina Clément explains.

The core collection consists of trompe-l'œil desserts: individual sculptures that replicate the appearance of fruit.

In its first stage of development, the project operates as a premium artisanal pastry laboratory focused on small-batch, made-to-order production, with customers collecting their orders directly from the workshop.

World.title: Kosovo Probes Alleged Police Violence Against Serb During Raid
World.content:
North Mitrovica Hospital , Kosovo, where the man received treatment. Photo: BIRN.

Kosovo’s Police Inspectorate said on Wednesday that it was investigating reports published on August 11 claiming officers used excessive force against a Serb man, Nenad Raskovic, during a raid at his home near the northern municipality of Zubin Potok.

Photographs shared on media and social networks show injuries on Raskovic’s back.

The Police Inspectorate, IPK, said it had interviewed Raskovic at North Mitrovica Hospital, where he is receiving treatment.

“The IPK has initiated this preliminary investigation with the aim of verifying the allegations and clarifying all relevant facts and circumstances related to the case,” the Inspectorate, an independent institution overseeing police conduct, said in a statement.

The Inspectorate said it would take all necessary steps, including “cooperating with relevant institutions, obtaining official documents and information, and interviewing people who may have knowledge of the incident”.

The Belgrade-backed Kosovo Serb party, Srpska Lista, said Raskovic said police officers entered his home in Dren village on Tuesday and, after searching the property, began hitting him without explanation.

“After that, Nenad was left tied to a tree. With the help of friends, he was freed and taken to the Family Medicine Centre in Zubin Potok, and then to the Clinical Hospital Centre in Mitrovica,” the party said.

In interviews given to media from hospital, Raskovic alleged that he was beaten by Kosovo police.

The Srpska List party called on Western embassies and organisations, NATO-led peacekeepers in KFOR and the EU rule-of-law mission EULEX to “examine the allegations and take action within their respective mandates to establish the facts and ensure the rights and safety of citizens”.

Petar Petkovic, head of the Serbian government’s office for Kosovo, also posted photos of the alleged injuries inflicted by Kosovo police on Tuesday, saying that “these are photos of [Kosovo Prime Minister Albin] Kurti’s ‘democracy’.

“For weeks, months and years, we have been warning the entire international community about the persecution of Serbs by Kurti’s regime, which has led to this. When those responsible face no sanctions and there is no adequate protection, these are the consequences,” Petkovic wrote.

Kosovo Police confirmed searching Raskovic’s home. Erduan Baliqi, a police spokesperson for the North Region, told BIRN: “Raskovic’s house was among the properties searched during the operation in Dren village… The searches were related to information on weapons.”

Baliqi said the police had “no information about the use of violence”.

Civil society organisations in Serb-majority northern Kosovo have called on the European Union to assess EULEX’s monitoring of the Kosovo Police.

“These allegations require an urgent and independent investigation, as well as an appropriate response from the relevant institutions,” they said in a statement.

The allegations come as attention focuses on war-related crimes in the Zubin Potok area, where excavations have been carried out in several villages in search of mass graves.

So far, remains believed to belong to four people have been exhumed, while three people have been arrested on suspicion of war crimes against civilians.

World.title: New Hungarian President Elected; Vows to Restore the Rule of Law
World.content:
Hungary cannot be built on “vengeance” and building a new future for it “demands both justice and self-restraint”, Hungary’s new president, Andras Baka, said after being elected by the ruling Tisza party’s 140 votes in parliament on Tuesday evening.

The former governing party Fidesz boycotted the vote and called both the process and the new president illegitimate.

The 73-year-old will be sworn in to the largely ceremonial post on August 19 and will remain in office until Hungary’s new constitution is adopted – a process that could take up to five years. The new constitution is expected to pave the way for the direct election of the country’s next president. According to a poll conducted by Median last year, 66 per cent of Hungarians would prefer direct presidential elections, with only Fidesz voters backing the current system by a significant majority of 61 per cent.

Commentators see Baka, a former Supreme Court chief judge and two-term judge serving at the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) in Strasbourg, as a broadly acceptable candidate for a large majority of Hungarians: an experienced, respected man with solid legal credentials.

Baka was an outspoken critic of the regime of former prime minister Viktor Orban, which removed him from his position as president of the Supreme Court in 2012 after he criticised his judicial reforms, which included plans to transfer cases to more government-friendly judges.

The Orban government passed tailor-made legislation that would have required previous judicial experience in Hungary to become president of the Supreme Court. It was a condition that Baka did not meet, given much of his career had been spent at the ECHR. Baka sued the Orban government and won at the Court of Justice of the European Union’s (ECJ), but was not reinstated to his position.

His election by parliament puts an end to a somewhat embarrassing casting process by new Prime Minister Peter Magyar, whose first choice was Hungary’s renowned chess world champion Judit Polgar, but she politely declined the offer, partly because of controversial remarks made on social media, mostly concerning her silence on political issues.

Baka is clearly a more political choice, especially considering his experience and background. But his election also suggests that Magyar has been willing to choose a figure with a strong independent streak rather than a party loyalist, unlike the previous Fidesz-appointed incumbent, Tamas Sulyok, whose resignation Magyar had made a campaign promise.

“Andras Baka has had an outstanding and highly prestigious career, and he is a very autonomous person. I see his election as president as a possible sign of self-restraint on the part of Prime Minister Peter Magyar, who won a very broad mandate in the April 12 election,” Marta Pardavi, chair of the Hungarian Helsinki Committee, told BIRN.

Baka is distinctly different from influencer-style politicians like Magyar or even Health Minister Zsolt Hegedus, who skyrocketed to fame with his dancing after Tisza’s election victory. Baka is a calm, principled man who believes in core values such as democracy and the rule of law. “His election can send the message that Hungary takes its highest office seriously,” Pardavi added.

Baka himself has made clear that he does not intend to become a pliant partner for the government and will voice criticism when necessary. He has already been one of the leading critics of the Tisza government’s recent constitutional amendment limiting MPs’ mandates to 12 years, arguing that it infringes on passive voting rights – in other words, that it restricts voters’ choice of candidates.

In his speech to parliament on Tuesday, Baka said that the nation had “wasted an entire generation”, and has fallen from being a frontrunner in 1990 to one of the countries lagging behind in the region. He described the country’s situation as critical in areas such as the rule of law, health care, education, child protection, energy and transport.

But he also warned that “an election result in itself cannot restore the rule of law.” The rule of law, he argued, does not only imply that institutions work, but also that people can trust that the rules apply to everyone, without exception.

Baka is also in keeping with Magyar’s conservative background, having served as an MP in Hungary’s first democratically elected parliament after 1990 as part of the Hungarian Democratic Forum (although he never formally joined the party). He used to work with Laszlo Solyom, who later became president and was the last head of state to use the office as a check on the government and openly criticise its policies.

World.title: North Macedonia Parties Share Out Nearly €9 Million from State Budget
World.content:
North Macedonia’s political parties received almost 9 million euros from the state budget this year for their regular operations, with the ruling VMRO DPMNE party taking a record 2.5 million euros and the main opposition Social Democrats, SDSM, seeing its funding fall by around 40 per cent to about 1 million euros.

A BIRN analysis of the 2026 payments, based on data obtained from the Ministry of Justice, shows that the three largest recipients, VMRO DPMNE, the SDSM and the ethnic Albanian Democratic Union for Integration, DUI, together received about 45 per cent of the total funding.

Adding in the smaller Levica [Left] and ZNAM parties, more than half of the money went to just five parties.

The DUI received about 472,000 euros, down from about 840,000 euros last year.

Both falls and rises reflect the parties’ performance in the 2025 local elections and the number of municipal councillors they secured.

North Macedonia’s system ties state funding to electoral performance.

Thirty per cent of the available money is distributed equally among parties and coalitions that meet a 1-per-cent electoral threshold. The other 70 per cent is allocated according to the number of elected MPs and municipal councillors.

This makes local elections particularly important. While parliament has 120 seats, the country’s municipalities have 1,307 elected councillors. In the 2025 local elections, the VMRO DPMNE-led coalition won 548 council seats, compared with 231 for the SDSM-led coalition.

“A councillor and an MP are worth the same, so this explains the competition to get as many councillors as possible,” a source from one of the parties told BIRN under condition of anonymity.

The system acts as an important financial incentive for smaller parties without any MPs, or even any councillors, as they can still qualify for some state funding simply by passing the 1-per-cent threshold in any single municipality during local elections.

In some of the smaller municipalities in local elections, that threshold can be crossed by winning only a few dozen votes.

BIRN previously reported on how seven smaller parties exploited this feature to secure more than 80,000 euros each for the following four years. In some cases, such parties run alone in just one, or in a few, municipalities to reach this threshold, while at national level remaining part of coalitions led by big parties.

Overall, 62 parties qualified for regular state funding in 2026, the data show, although around one-third of them received less than 20,000 euros.

Apart from the almost 9 million euros in annual funding, which consumed 0.15 per cent of the state budget, the state also reimburses party election campaign expenses and provides additional annual funding for the research centres of the four parties with the strongest electoral results.

In 2026, an additional 320,000 euros was allocated for those research centres, shared between VMRO DPMNE, the SDSM, the DUI and Levica.

The funding comes with obligations, such as submitting annual financial statements and reports and declaring any donations to the State Audit Office, which oversees use of the funds.

The law requires the parties to publish these financial reports on their websites by the end of each April. In reality, this requirement is frequently ignored, according to BIRN’s analysis.

The State Audit Office told BIRN that the law does not clearly designate who is responsible for monitoring this obligation. Another issue is that parties are not legally required to have an official website.

The Audit Office said they have begun discussing digitalisation of parties’ financial reporting, including the possibility of creating a single online platform where all the parties would publish their financial reports.

World.title: Letter from London: From Burnham’s Bounce to Ghost Ships in the Danube
World.content:
Greetings from London, where we are all enjoying, or at least experiencing, the “Burnham Bounce”.

No, it’s not an expensive hairstyle, a dance move, isometric exercise, or body modification. It’s a lift in the opinion polls for the ruling Labour Party.

It’s attributed to the easy, breezy style of its new leader, our new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, whose relatively jargon-free form of communications has lifted his party out of its former doldrums to the stratospheric-sounding level of 28 per cent support in the polls.

There was a time when the two ‘big beasts’ of the British party system, the Labour and Conservative parties, both cruised along at around 40 per cent in the polls. That left the small fry – mainly Liberals and various nationalists – to fight over the remaining 20 per cent.

But times have changed. These days, 28 per cent is a stellar achievement for one of the two major parties.

World.title: US Right-Wing Heritage Foundation Promotes Changes to Bosnia’s Peace Agreement
World.content:
A report published in February by Germany’s Der Spiegel, Sweden’s Aftonbladet and the environmental campaign group BLOOM detailed what BLOOM described as “harmful links between the European conservative right and Trumpist circles”, indicating that some European parliamentarians have come under American influence as Washington attempts to shift the political balance in Brussels rightwards.

BLOOM researcher Alessandro Mazzotti told BIRN that the Heritage Foundation’s isn’t just seeking political connections on the far right of the European parliament, but also within European People’s Party, EPP, which brings together centre-right parties and is the largest political group in the EU.

The report also highlights a meeting between Manfred Weber, president of the EPP, Jorgen Warborn, a member of the Swedish Parliament, and representatives of the Heritage Foundation.

“The Heritage Foundation acts as a kind of intermediary in this shift of the EPP toward a more radically right-wing position,” said Mazzotti.

An important figure connecting people within this lobbying environment, Mazzotti claimed, is Croatian MEP Zeljana Zovko of the centre-right Croatian Democratic Union party, which is part of the EPP. He claimed that Zovko has opened many doors for the Heritage Foundation.

Zovko provided support for the Heritage Foundation’s TradFest in Zagreb. “Over the past three or four years she has been one of the leading representatives in the European Parliament for the European People’s Party. Essentially the first point of contact between the EPP and Heritage. She was really the person who started this cooperation, this dialogue,” said Mazzotti.

Zovko has publicly met with Heritage representatives on multiple occasions, including Primorac.

According to Mazzotti, Zovko is the first person to have created the link between the Heritage Foundation and the EPP – a link that today influences cooperation between Brussels and the Trump administration.

Zovko told BIRN that critical sentiment towards her is partly caused by her role in the EU’s trade agreement with the US, as well as her role as the EPP’s chief negotiator in Brussels’ talks with Washington.

“I am the EPP negotiator, that is why I am also in the area of defence and trade and that is why all the attacks are there. I am the contact person for Congress and all the [American] foundations. I am the key person in the EPP for relations with everyone in the US Congress and I talk to all the foundations,” she said.

“As the vice-president of the EPP group in charge of EPP diplomacy, my duty includes maintaining contacts with all the relevant interlocutors. I open the doors and that is my nature – you have to communicate with everyone, not only with Heritage and America First, but also with the left foundations,” she added.

In her view, a revision of the Dayton Agreement is not currently a realistic option.

“I advocate for full implementation, respect for the Dayton Agreement and the spirit of the Dayton Agreement. It is not being respected; if it were, Croats would have their own member of the presidency and they would have a fair electoral law,” she said.

Critics have alleged that the election victory of the current Croat member of the tripartite Bosnian presidency, Zeljko Komsic, relied on more Bosniak voters rather than Croats, and hence does not represent the will of the Croat people in the country.

However, as Zovko pointed out: “For a revision [of Dayton], you need to have the other two peoples [Serbs and Bosniaks] on your side. The Serbs would not agree to that, and the Bosniaks in this set-up would not agree to a more profound revision either.”

World.title: Kosovo Pays the Price as Serbia Stalls Cross-Border Electricity Transmissions
World.content:
Amid an ongoing energy crisis and mounting financial costs, Kosovo has renewed its call on the European Union and the Energy Community for South East Europe to pressure Serbia to make cross-border transmission capacity available, after Belgrade again failed to meet its commitment to do so.

The Energy Community, a Vienna-based international organisation that oversees compliance and dispute resolution in the energy sector across the Western Balkans and the Black Sea region, set a July 1 deadline for Serbia to provide Kosovo with cross-border transmission capacities.

The ultimatum, which stemmed from a Ministerial Council decision, reminded Belgrade of its need to “ensure compliance with Energy Community law”.

World.title: Montenegro Police Raid Nets 50 Foreigners, ‘Hundreds’ of Digital Devices, and Cash
World.content:
Montenegrin police said on Tuesday they were checking on more than 50 foreign nationals, most of them Ukrainian citizens, who they found when raiding a large house in the Mareza area of Podgorica.

Police also said they seized hundreds of digital devices, “sophisticated equipment” and a large amount of cash.

“Police officers, based on previously undertaken proactive activities, located and identified the facility – a large house in Mareza, Podgorica – after which they entered the building in accordance with the law,” a Police Directorate statement said.

According to police, they found more than 50 foreign nationals inside the house and carried out a search of the premises, documenting equipment and other material relevant to the investigation.

“During the activities, several hundred digital devices and other elements of sophisticated equipment were found, and their quantity and scale were such that, for adequate relocation, they had to be transported by a cargo motor vehicle,” police said.

Police said a large amount of cash was also found and that its origin and possible connection to the activities under investigation would be checked.

The authorities said they were examining the legal basis on which the foreigners are staying and working in Montenegro, their activities and movements, the purpose and manner of use of the seized equipment and devices, and any possible links to illegal activities.

“Given the complexity of the case, the director of the Police Directorate has formed an Operational Team composed of several groups of police officers specialised in cyber security and high-tech crime, financial investigations and money laundering, international operational cooperation, as well as foreigner and migration affairs, with the strong support of the National Security Agency,” the statement said.

Police added that they were taking action in coordination with the State Prosecutor’s Office to establish all the facts and could not comment further at this stage..

“Having in mind the interest of the proceedings and the complexity of the criminal investigation, the Police Directorate is not in a position at this moment to provide more details, so as not to jeopardise the further course of the preliminary investigation,” the statement said.

World.title: Serbian Firefighters Douse Wildfire in Deliblato Sands After Seven-Day Blaze
World.content:
A fire blazing in Serbia’s Deliblato Sands for seven days has finally been brought under control, Milos Milenkovic, Assistant Head of Serbia’s Fire and Rescue Units Directorate told the state broadcaster RTS on Tuesday.

The Deliblato Sands, Deliblatska Pescara in Serbian, is the largest continental sandy terrain in Europe, covering around 350 square km in southeast Vojvodina, Serbia’s northern province – a nature reserve nicknamed Europe’s Sahara.

The wildfire broke out amid an intense heatwave and prolonged drought affecting Serbia and much of the Balkans, with temperatures reaching around 40 degrees Celsius. The hot and dry conditions, coupled with strong winds, have significantly increased the risk of wildfires and complicated firefighting efforts.

World.title: Accommodation Owners Claim Croatian Local Host Campaign Started Late
World.content:
August the 12th, 2026 – The Croatian Tourist Board is satisfied, but accommodation owners are claiming that the Croatian Local Host campaign started too late.

“We’re extremely satisfied with the results of the first Local Host label campaign,” stated Kristjan Staničić, director of the Croatian National Tourist Board (HTZ). Croatia very successfully recorded 12.4 million arrivals from the beginning of the year to the end of July.

Ana Roksandic/Poslovni reports that eight million impressions and almost 500 completed reservations are the results of the first joint promotional campaign by the Croatian National Tourist Board and the Booking.com platform dedicated to Croatian family accommodation and hosts gathered under the Croatian Your Host/Local Host label.

The campaign “Experience real Croatia” ran during the months of June and July on the markets of Germany, Austria, Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary. At its heart were the actual local hosts themselves and the authentic experiences they offer their guests, the Croatian National Tourist Board (HTZ) announced.

room for improvement

So far, over 3,570 properties with over 21,170 beds have joined the Croatian Local Host project. The largest number of properties with the Local Host label are located in Istria, on the Kvarner and in Split-Dalmatia County. Looking by destination, the highest numbers are in Crikvenica, Dubrovnik, Pula, Rovinj and Medulin.

“All of our activities are aimed at protecting genuine family accommodation that has been building Croatian tourism for generations and giving special value to our tourism offer. These hosts are precisely the foundation of Croatian tourism, which is why their protection will continue to be our focus,” revealed Tonči Glavina, Minister of Tourism and Sport, adding: “For the first time, we ‘ve also carried out a national promotional campaign dedicated exclusively to family accommodation, and the first results are already visible through 6 percent better occupancy, which confirms that the market recognises the value of authentic hospitality.”

the coast, of course, dominates the campaign

The largest number of properties with the Local Host label are situated in Istria, on the Kvarner and in Split-Dalmatia County.

As HTZ stated on its official website, the “Your Host” (Local Host) label enables hosts to stand out among numerous private accommodation providers and reach guests looking for an authentic and hospitable experience. Label holders can also use the official Local Host visual identity, and their offer can be included in HTZ promotional activities on foreign markets and digital channels. The label also provides them with guidelines for further raising the quality and sustainability of their business. However, among family accommodation providers there are also questions about the criteria for obtaining the label and its real impact.

“In fact, this label tries to make a distinction between such hosts and landlords where the guest often has no contact with the host at all. They arrive, get a code for the key, enter the apartment and leave, and you practically don’t even know who stayed in your accommodation. When you have the Local Host label, you should be present in the place where the property is located. Not necessarily at the address itself, but you should live, or have your residence, in that town or place. If, for example, you rent out a holiday home in Šibenik-Knin County and live in Split, you will not be able to get that label, regardless of the fact that you are available to the guest in that holiday home.

The reason is that your address of residence is not in the municipality or city where the property is located. Obviously there is still a little room for fine-tuning there, but there are people who already have that label and who work exactly like that – they are truly present and available to their guests,” said Ante Glavaš, vice-president of the Croatian Association of Family Accommodation (HUOS), adding: “However, some people in residential buildings have also received these labels. On what principle that happened is not clear to us.”

has this label led to higher occupancy rates?

HTZ says the label leads to higher occupancy: “In addition to an initially higher occupancy rate, properties that are part of the Local Host programme in 2025 recorded further positive progression: their occupancy grew by 5.74 percent compared to the previous year, while the occupancy of properties that are not part of the programme grew by only 0.6 percent. In the first five months of 2026 the occupancy of properties that are part of the Local Host programme, both in absolute terms and in terms of growth rate, remains higher compared to properties that are not in the programme relative to the same period of the previous year.”

However, one label holder we spoke to said the campaign did not have a particularly promotional effect on her property because it was carried out during June and July. Olinka Gjigaš, director of the Tourist Board of the City of Križevci and holder of the “Your Host” label in the Municipality of Kalnik, stressed that she is speaking from personal experience about the campaign’s impact: “I can’t really say there were any changes because the campaign started quite late. At the time when the promotion was being filmed, I already had 90 percent of the dates booked. I saw that the minister spoke about six percent growth, which surprised me – I wonder how that was even calculated.”

HTZ, however, rates the campaign results significantly more positively. “We’re extremely satisfied with the results of the first Local Host label campaign on the Booking.com platform, as well as with the overall effect of the promotional activities aimed at this label so far,” said Kristjan Staničić, director of HTZ, adding that the Local Host project is continuously gathering an ever larger number of hosts. HTZ will continue promotional activities in the second half of the year, when a new wave of the campaign on the domestic market will follow from mid-August to the end of October.

5.74 percen is how much the occupancy of Croatian Local Host properties grew compared to last year, which arguably isn’t much.

istria takes the lead

In a broader context, the Local Host results come at a time when Croatian tourism has been constantly recording a positive continuation of the season. According to data from the eVisitor and eCrew systems, from the beginning of the year to the end of July Croatia recorded 12.4 million arrivals and 59.1 million overnight stays, which is one percent more than in the same period last year. On the Adriatic 56.1 million overnight stays were recorded, or 0.5 percent more, while on the continent, including Zagreb, more than three million overnight stays were recorded, with growth of one percent.

In July alone, 4.7 million arrivals and 29.6 million overnight stays were recorded. Compared to July last year, the number of arrivals increased by 2.5 percent and the number of overnight stays by one percent. The most guests came from Germany, Slovenia, Croatia, Poland, the Czech Republic, Austria and Hungary.

Istria retained its leading position among the counties with 16.7 million overnight stays in the first seven months, followed by Split-Dalmatia County with 11.1 million and Kvarner with 9.7 million overnight stays. Among destinations, Dubrovnik, Rovinj, Poreč, Split and Umag lead.

World.title: June Sees Drop in Overnight Stays in Croatian Commercial Accommodation
World.content:
August the 12th, 2026 – June saw a drop in overnight stays in Croatian commercial accommodation recorded, with Istria County outperforming the rest of the country.

A mixed picture could be garnered when looking at overnight stays realised in Croatian commercial accommodation facilities in June this year. Jutarnji reports that a total of 3.0 million tourist arrivals and 13.5 million overnight stays were recorded. Compared to June 2025, tourist arrivals were down by 6.6% and overnight stays by 6.1%, according to the Croatian Bureau of Statistics (DZS).

the germans (of course) lead the way

Of the total overnight stays realised, domestic tourists accounted for 8.9% and foreign tourists for 91.1%. Domestic tourists recorded 387 thousand arrivals and 1.2 million overnight stays, which is 11.8% more arrivals and 11.7% more overnight stays than back in June 2025. Foreign tourists recorded 2.6 million arrivals and 12.3 million overnight stays, which is 8.9% fewer arrivals and 7.5% fewer overnight stays than back in June 2025.

The highest number of overnight stays realised by foreign tourists in June 2026 was achieved by tourists from Germany, totalling 2.7 million overnight stays, or 22.1% of all foreign overnight stays. Compared to June 2025, their overnight stays were down by 28.1%. On average, they recorded 7.7 overnight stays per arrival.

After German tourists, the largest shares of foreign overnight stays were held by tourists from Austria (10.3%), Slovenia (9.9%), Poland (8.8%), the Czech Republic (6.6%), the United Kingdom (5.3%) and Italy (3.8%). Compared to June 2025, increases in overnight stays were recorded by tourists from Italy (5.0%), Slovenia (3.9%), Poland (3.2%), the Czech Republic (2.4%) and the United Kingdom (1.2%), while tourists from Austria had 6.0% fewer overnight stays.

istria county outperformed the rest of the country in june this year

In June 2026, Istria County once again recorded the highest number of overnight stays in the country, totalling 4.3 million, or 31.9% of all overnight stays in Croatia. Despite being the county with the most tourist overnight stays, overnight stays in Istria County fell by 10.0% compared to June 2025. Domestic tourists in Istria County recorded 219 thousand overnight stays (15.9% more than in June 2025), while foreign tourists recorded 4.1 million overnight stays (down 11.1% from the previous year’s June).

After Istria County came Split-Dalmatia County with 2.7 million overnight stays (20.0% of the Croatian total) and Primorje-Gorski Kotar County with 2.2 million (16.4%). Compared to June 2025, overnight stays were down 7.5% in Primorje-Gorski Kotar County and 1.7% in Split-Dalmatia County.

In June 2026, the highest number of overnight stays was recorded by tourists in two age groups: those under 14 years of age and those between 55 and 64 years of age. Each of these groups recorded 2.2 million overnight stays, accounting for 16.2% of the total.

World.title: More and More Filipinos Are Working in Croatia
World.content:
August the 12th, 2026 – More and more Filipinos are being registered as living and working in Croatia, with the vast majority employed in the tourism and trade sectors.

As Jadranka Dozan/Poslovni reports, over the first seven months of this year, a total of 106,400 permits were issued to citizens of third countries (countries outside of the EEA), of which almost two-thirds were for work in tourism and construction.

The number of issued work permits is reportedly falling, but Interior Ministry data doesn’t show the real number of workers from abroad. The latest data from the Ministry of the Interior on permits issued to foreign workers from so-called third countries only confirmed the continuation of the year-on-year decline in their overall number. This is partly a consequence of the fact that since March last year the maximum duration of permits has been extended from one to three years.

this “decline” isn’t straightforward

How much of this alleged decline is explained by that change in legal rules, and how much is contributed by generally tightened rules or some other reasons (such as meeting part of the need for workers through increased work engagement of domestic pensioners or, for example, returnees to Croatia), the Interior Ministry statistics don’t reveal.

In the first seven months of 2026, a total of 106,400 residence and work permits were issued to citizens of “third countries”, which is 7.5 percent less than last year. Looking only at July, almost 23 percent fewer were issued than last year.

seasonal employment

So far in 2026, the share of permits for seasonal jobs increased significantly, they’re actually up by 40 percent compared to last year – while those for new employment are down 31 percent, and permit extensions are up around 10 percent. Looking only at the month of July, Interior Ministry data reveals that a total of 12,282 positive decisions were issued for imported labour (compared to 15,905 in the same month last year). Almost every fourth of these, or more than 3,000 permits, was given for seasonal work, while just over 9,000 relate to new employment (just under 4,500) and permit extensions (just under 4,800).

40 percent is how much the number of permits for seasonal jobs has risen this year compared to last year, and it’s far from insignificant. Looking at the situation by activity, almost two-thirds of permits go to the two sectors where the import of workers is normally the most massive, tourism and hospitality, as well as construction. This applies both to those issued last month and to the total number issued since the beginning of the year. However, in construction there are 17 percent fewer this year than in the first seven months of last year, while in tourism and hospitality activities there are 5.4 percent more.

Of the other three most represented sectors when it comes to importing workers, an increase in the number of issued permits in 2026 is recorded only in trade. This also contributes to changes in the structure of issued permits in terms of the origin of workers. By far the largest growth is recorded for those issued to Filipinos – almost 50 percent higher than last year. Filipino workers, in addition to the tourism sector, are most often engaged by employers from the trade sector.

misleading statistics

The Interior Ministry’s records of work permits, however, fail to reveal many things and are certainly not the best indicator of the real situation regarding how many workers from third countries there are in Croatia. Experts on migration and demography have been pointing out the problem of recording foreign workers in general for a long time.

On the occasion of the recent publication of data by the Croatian Bureau of Statistics on migration for 2025, one of the more active among them, Tado Jurić, once again warned about the methodological challenges in this area. From the official data of the Interior Ministry and the CBS (according to which 56,700 immigrated foreign citizens were recorded last year), no one can say with certainty how many of them are actually in Croatia because these are records of different phenomena, he says.

For that reason, the number of insured persons in the Croatian Pension Insurance Institute (HZMO) is usually considered a somewhat more authoritative indicator. In its records in the middle of this year there were a little under 151,000 insured persons who are citizens of third countries (more precisely, with travel documents of those countries), which is about 29,000 more than at the end of last year. Although these are insured persons (which does not automatically mean employees), this is still roughly the indicator closest to reality, and it roughly implies that every 12th person who works and/or pays contributions in Croatia is a foreigner.

“practically half of croatia’s foreign workforce comes from africa and asia”

Given that practically half of the foreign workforce in Croatia today comes from Asia and Africa, migration experts have long emphasised that this requires active management of the processes, both in the context of integration and policies aimed at stronger activation of one’s own potentials. Due to low labour productivity in the public sector, it is often pointed out that there are certain employment reserves there for the entrepreneurial sector, but reforms of that kind do not come easily.

World.title: Almost All Istrian Beaches Have Excellent Quality Seawater
World.content:
August the 12th, 2026 – Almost all Istrian beaches have excellent quality seawater according to the latest measurements, with only four lagging behind.

The sea at Istrian beaches continues to be of exceptionally high quality. In the sixth examination of this year, conducted from the 28th of July to the 6th of August, as many as 98.2 percent of the seawater samples received an excellent rating. Index reports that the sea was sampled at a total of 222 measuring points on beaches from Savudrija to Brestova.

During the process of seawater sampling, the sea temperature ranged between 24 and 29 degrees, while the air temperature was from 24 to 33 degrees.

only four locations were less than exceptional

Excellent swimming seawater quality was recorded at 218 measuring points. Good quality was also recorded at one location, in Ližnjan at Matićev Pisk below the hotel. At three locations, the sea received a satisfactory rating only. These are AC Kažela – FKK in Medulin, Tarska vala in the Tar-Vabriga area, and the location near Hotel Molindrio in Poreč.

bacteria measuring

When examining the seawater, the quantities of intestinal enterococci and the bacterium Escherichia coli are determined as indicators of microbiological pollution. During the sampling process, meteorological conditions, sea temperature and salinity, as well as any visible pollution, are also recorded.

Based on the results of individual samples, the sea is classified as excellent, good or satisfactory. The results of all individual examinations are available via the online application of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Green Transition.

World.title: eVisitor Just Recorded the Best July in Croatia in the Past Two Years
World.content:
August the 11th, 2026 – The widely praised eVisitor system just recorded the best July in Croatia in the past two years, with enviable numbers of both arrivals and overnight stays.

According to the latest data from the eVisitor system, which records tourist traffic achieved in commercial and non-commercial facilities as well as nautical charter (eCrew system), Croatia recorded 12.4 million arrivals and 59.1 million overnight stays in the period from January to the end of July. Poslovni reports that when compared to the same period last year, this represents growth of 1 percent in arrivals and in overnight stays. Of that total, 56.1 million overnight stays were achieved on the Adriatic, a rise of 0.5 percent compared to last year, while the continent, including the city of Zagreb, recorded more than 3 million overnight stays, which is 1 percent more than last year.

4.7 million arrivals and 29.6 million overnight stays

eVisitor data also show that during July this year Croatia recorded an extremely impressive 4.7 million arrivals and 29.6 million overnight stays, which compared to July last year represents growth of 2.5 percent in arrivals and 1 percent in overnight stays.

In the seventh month the largest number of guests came from the markets of Germany, Slovenia, Croatia, Poland, the Czech Republic, Austria, Hungary and others. By counties, the most tourists were counted in Istria, Split-Dalmatia County and Kvarner, while among individual destinations the most visited were Rovinj, Vir, Poreč, Medulin and Dubrovnik.

“We’re more than satisfied with the tourist results achieved throughout the first seven months of this year, and especially with the fact that in July we achieved the best result in the last two years. This confirms that Croatian tourism continues to maintain its competitiveness and resilience and that, despite changes in the market, we are succeeding in maintaining positive trends. It is particularly pleasing that we are also recording good results in financial indicators. In July the value of fiscalised invoices rose by 18 percent, while the number of issued invoices was 8 percent higher compared to the same month last year. We are also recording growth in road, air and maritime traffic, and all these results confirm that we have responded well to market circumstances – both through quality promotion of Croatia and through timely adjustment of the offer.

I’d like to sincerely thank the entire tourism sector for the effort invested, and especially accommodation providers who responded to our appeals and with their special offers additionally contributed to the competitiveness of our offer. Ahead of us is still a good part of August after which we will make a complete overview of this main part of the tourist year. Croatian tourism is once again confirming its strength this year, and the results achieved show that we are on the right path and that together we are successfully responding to changes and challenges,” said Tonči Glavina, Minister of Tourism and Sport.

the situation on a county by county basis

When Croatia’s tourist results are segmented by counties, in the first seven months the most overnight stays were achieved in Istria (16.7 million overnight stays), Split-Dalmatia County (11.1 million overnight stays) and Kvarner (9.7 million overnight stays), while by destinations the leaders were Dubrovnik, Rovinj, Poreč, Split and Umag.

“The course and results of the tourist year so far show that Croatia still has a very strong position on the global tourism market, despite all the demanding circumstances. What we particularly read from this year’s tourist movements is a change in the way guests make decisions about their travels. Last-minute reservations play an important role, and when choosing a destination the best value for money is increasingly sought, along with safety and easy accessibility.

croatia’s enviable geographical position as a massive aid

In this context Croatia has a series of advantages: from proximity to our most important source markets and good transport connections to the diversity of the offer that enables different types of holidays. The results achieved therefore give us additional wind in our sails for the continuation of the tourist year, all the more so as the period of Ferragosto is ahead of us, traditionally very important for the travel of Italian guests. In addition to the main summer months, we are also recording excellent announcements for the post-season, for which promotional activities start in mid-August, especially on the markets of Poland and the United Kingdom,” said Kristjan Staničić, director of the Croatian National Tourist Board.

Viewed by markets, during the first seven months the most overnight stays were achieved by guests from the markets of Germany (10.3 million overnight stays), Croatia (7.6 million overnight stays), Slovenia (6.7 million overnight stays), Austria (4.3 million overnight stays), Poland (3.9 million overnight stays), the Czech Republic (3 million overnight stays), the UK (2.2 million overnight stays), Hungary (2.1 million overnight stays) and others.

World.title: Croatian Public Debt Rises by 4.6 Billion Euros in a Single Year
World.content:
August the 11th, 2026 – Croatian public debt has increased by 4.6 billion euros in a single year, with long-term borrowing dominating the entire picture.

As Poslovni/Ana Blaskovic writes, Croatian public debt stood at a whopping 55 billion euros back at the end of April, which is 4.6 billion euros or 9 percent higher than in the same period last year, according to the latest data from the Croatian National Bank (HNB). Compared to the end of last year, the debt increased by 2.7 billion euros, or 5.2 percent, while on a monthly basis a slight decrease of 148 million euros was recorded.

The largest sum of the increase comes from stronger borrowing by the central government, whose debt reached 54 billion euros. This means the central government accounts for more than 98 percent of Croatia’s total public debt. At the same time, local government units, municipalities, cities and counties, are borrowing more and more. Their obligations have been rising for 15 consecutive months, and at double-digit rates.

the domination of long-term borrowing

Back in April, the annual growth rate stood at 21.4 percent, after 20 percent in March. In contrast, social security funds continued to reduce their debt level, which was 32.2 percent lower on an annual basis.

The structure of borrowing shows that long-term instruments still prevail. About 65 percent of the non-consolidated debt relates to bonds, while the rest consists of loans, deposits and short-term securities. Notably, the Ministry of Finance has significantly increased the issuance of treasury bills, which is why domestic debt in the short-term securities segment rose by 45.5 percent year-on-year, Raiffeisen analysts note.

Croatia continues to finance itself mostly on the domestic market. At the end of April, domestic investors held 68.6 percent of the public debt, while the share of foreign creditors was 31.4 percent. After Eurozone accession, the share of the domestic component stabilised around 70 percent, reflecting a multi-year trend of strengthening domestic sources of state financing.

the public invests 4.9 billion euros in a year

HNB data also show growth in investments from the general public in government securities. Household investments increased from 3.9 billion euros to 4.9 billion euros in one single year, while financial companies raised their exposure to state debt from 31.1 billion euros to 32.6 billion euros. Despite the rise in nominal debt, Croatia remains below the Maastricht threshold. At the end of the first quarter, the public debt-to-GDP ratio stood at 58.4 percent, 0.2 percentage points higher than a year earlier.

Raiffeisen analyst Petar Bejuk assesses that domestic fiscal indicators remain more favourable than the wider Eurozone average, primarily thanks to strong nominal economic growth. For the full year, he expects the public debt ratio to stay below 60 percent of GDP, noting that fiscal policy should preserve enough room to respond to possible future risks.

World.title: Ancient Greek Treasure Over 2,000 Years Old Found in Attic in Trogir
World.content:
August the 11th, 2026 – An ancient Greek treasure over 2,000 years old was discovered by change in an attic in Trogir. Meet the Trogir Kairos.

Have you heard of the Trogir Kairos? It is a beautiful ancient Greek marble relief from the 4th or 3rd century BC depicting the god Kairos. The work is considered an exceptional artistic achievement and one of the rare surviving sculptural representations of this Greek deity.

this fascinating relief ended up in an attic in trogir, but how?!

Even today, almost 100 after its discovery, debates continue about its journey and just how it ended up sitting in an attic in a Dalmatian coastal town. Poslovni reports that the ancient artwork, created by Lysippos, one of the greatest sculptors of antiquity, was found in the attic of a house belonging to a prominent Trogir family. According to multiple experts, it was brought from Greece up to nearby Croatia during the Renaissance period. Whether those who brought it knew its true value remains an open question and will never be answered.

The precious relief was discovered in the attic of a house that once belonged to the Statilić (Statileo) family, which produced several notable figures — diplomats, artists connected to the Hungarian-Croatian court, and world travellers. Historians therefore believe that one of the family members found the relief while travelling and brought it back to Trogir. It was discovered there in 1928 by the Trogir art historian Don Ivan Delalle.

who is the greek god kairos?

In Greek mythology, Kairos was the youngest son of Zeus, known as the god of the fleeting, brief moment. According to the myth, Kairos, who symbolises the right and decisive moment, must be seized by the lock of hair on his forehead before he flies away. The young god, depicted by Lysippos with wings on his feet and back, barely ever touches the ground, conveying his sheer speed. He reminds mere mortals that the right moment passes quickly and that opportunities do not return.

Kairos has no hair on the back of his head, symbolising the transience of chances: once he has passed by, he can no longer be grasped, and a missed moment cannot ever be recovered. This utterly remarkable relief from Trogir is regarded as one of the best-preserved and rarest depictions of the Greek god Kairos in the entire world.

World.title: Omiš Returns to its Pirate Past With a Real Spectacle at Sea on August 18th!
World.content:
August the 11th, 2026 – Located in the very heart of central Dalmatia, Omiš is closely connected to the world of the pirate, and the 18th of August promises an absolute spectacle at sea.

Omiš is set to honour its pirate past on August the 18th after a six year break. Marking its victory over the Venetian Empire from the 13th century, an incredible evening of history, local heritage, fireworks and entertainment awaits. This event is much anticipated and will lure in thousands of spectators keen for a trip back in time to the Omiš of old with the legendary leader of the local pirates, Malduh Kačić, at the helm.

why is this event so important?

If you’ve ever been to Dalmatia (and particularly if you’ve sailed along the heavily indented coastline and islands), you may have asked how the country fared back during the days when marauding pirates ruled the Adriatic. Turning the pages of the history book (a long way) back, we find ourselves in an era where piracy wasn’t nearly as frowned upon as it is today. Back then, it was a legitimate business that only the brave dared try their hand (or sword) at.

Along the heavily indented, cove-ridden rocks of the Dalmatian coast, the tradition of piracy goes back even further. It was noted way back during the reign of the various Illyrian tribes that used to live there before the ethnic Croatians arrived.

a hard lesson for venice…

Across the Adriatic Sea, the mighty and somewhat problematic Venetian Empire was very wary of the pirates from Croatia’s Neretva basin. Dominating Adriatic trade, Venice stacked up its enemies and had good reason to keep looking over its proverbial shoulder.

Indeed, back in 887 AD, a battle near Makarska between the Venetians and the so-called Narentine pirates took place, and during which Venetian Duke Pietro Candiano lost his life and his fleet was sunk to the watery depths below. After this event, the Venetians likely paid dearly for the freedom to travel and trade without encountering problems in the Croatian part of the Adriatic.

That relative ease didn’t last long, as the Omiš pirates (or gusari, if you want to truly go local) began disrupting it. That time period coincided with the rising prominence of the Kačić dynasty during the 12th century. This family didn’t have a tree. It was more like a forest. They were dukes and widely known for their ruthlessness and ruled over a large part of southern and central Dalmatia. Although they were officially the subjects of the Hungarian-Croatian king, they enjoyed plenty of autonomy. They opted to use that by organising professional piracy within their dominion.

keeping up with the Kačić family

This fearsome dynasty controlled the majority of the maritime traffic along the eastern Adriatic coast, and both Venetian and Ragusan (Dubrovnik) merchants had to pay up if they wanted to ensure their safe passage through that part of the sea. Just how far they were willing to go in their efforts to fully control that traffic is best explained by the fact that they were accused of attacking the vessels which took the Crusaders to the Palestine, and that even the Pope Honorius III started a war with the pirates, which he lost.

Every peace agreed upon with the Kačić family and Omiš pirates was short-lived, and it took almost two centuries to defeat them and establish safer passage along the Adriatic coast. The Kačić dynasty was eventually defeated and expelled from Omiš after the Venetians finally got the upper hand in 1287. Piracy lingered on, but it eventually weakened. By the time 1444 rolled around, Omiš ended up entirely occupied by the Venetians, and that marked the end of the tradition of piracy once and for all.

Thankfully, you can now freely sail in Dalmatia without any fear of being plundered, pillaged, or forced to pay for your safe passage, but it wasn’t always so peaceful!

Omiš takes us back to its pirate past on august the 18th

Now we’ve delved into the history of just why pirates are so significant to this part of the Dalmatian coast, we can look at what’s to come. After a six year break, Omiš is finally bringing back its beloved Pirate Battle. If you were to ask most people, they’d argue that it’s by far the Adriatic’s most spectacular historical reenactment, and it couldn’t possibly take place in a more apt location. On Tuesday the 18th of August, the Port of Omiš will shed all signs of modernity and totally transform into an authentic thirteenth-century battlefield.

Old vessels will cut across the water, cannons will drown out the summertime cicadas, swords will be drawn and fireworks will light up the blackness of the night sky above the Cetina canyon’s imposing rock faces. This is so much more than a show by the sea, it’s a living, accurate recreation of the moment when the fearless pirates of Omiš outsmarted the powerful and problematic Venice and cemented their rightful place in Dalmatian and indeed wider Croatian legend.

spectators will watch an ancient pirate battle from a modern setting

The last Pirate Battle took place in 2019, just before the coronavirus pandemic struck. An extremely extensive 15 million euro reconstruction of the Port of Omiš began soon after, forcing the event into a temporary pause. Now, the brand-new pier and seafront promenade are finally complete, offering the perfect stage for one of Croatia’s most atmospheric summer spectacles. You’ll be able to watch this ancient battle from a modern waterfront, witnessing heritage and history blend with modern Omiš in perfect harmony.

The newly renovated port and accompanying waterfront can comfortably host 10,000+ spectators, meaning that you’re guaranteed to find a spot from which you can enjoy the re-enactment and the rest of this marvellous event.

Around 150 costumed participants will take part in the upcoming event, with the local KPU Omiški gusari (Omiš Pirates Association) at the helm (no pun intended). They’ll be joined by allied historical groups from across the rest of Croatia: Kumpanija Vela Luka, the Dubrovački trombunjeri, the Klis Uskoks, Društvo Poljičana Sveti Jure – Priko, Bakar Town Guard 1848 and the Požega Town Guard. The event is being entirely organised by the Omiš Tourist Board, with great care paid both to historical accuracy and as a big “welcome back” to a much loved event.

what we can expect on the evening

The programme is set to begin early so that families with children and history lovers can soak up every moment.

18:30 – Activities for children on the waterfront will take place.

19:15 – A grand parade of all of the historical troops through the ancient streets of Omiš will delight all those gathered.

20:15 – The main event will begin, with the Pirate Battle itself in taking place in the ultra-modern, new port.

celebrations across the town

Immediately after that, the celebrations will continue with a performance by Kumpanija Vela Luka, ceremonial cannon fire from the famous Dubrovački trombunjeri (21:10), a dramatic fire show and an incredible fireworks display that will light up the entire harbour and the surrounding tall cliffs which make this town is instantly recognisable (21:40). Once those cannons eventually do fall silent, the celebrations will move to the Croatian Veterans’ Park. Organised by KPU Omiški gusari, the after-party features local food and drink, demonstrations of traditional crafts and a live concert by the popular band Vigor (21:50).

We can say with confidence that this is certainly the perfect way to bring an unforgettable Omiš summer evening to a close.

here’s a look at 2019’s event to get you prepared!

Should you need further information, look no further than here, and make sure to follow along on Instagram for more fantastic images and videos.

World.title: 55 signatures and counting for Ülle Madise's presidential bid; parties meet with Land, Madise
World.content:
Isamaa and Center Party held meetings with a potential presidential candidate, TalTech Rector Tiit Land on Wednesday. Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise will meet Isamaa, Center Party and Social Democrats on Monday.

Center Party representatives will meet Madise on Monday, party communications chief Andres Kalvik said. The Social Democrats have also scheduled a meeting for the same day, confirmed party communications head Ann‑Marii Nergi. Madise will also meet with Isamaa.

Riigikogu deputy speaker Toomas Kivimägi (Reform Party) said that collecting signatures for Madise began at 12:45 p.m. Wednesday, and she currently has 55.

Riigikogu esimees Lauri Hussar Ülle Madise kandidatuurile häält andmas Autor/allikas: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Those who have signed include members of the Reform Party, Estonia 200 and Social Democratic factions. Kivimägi noted that signatures from Isamaa are not expected yet, as they want to meet the potential presidential candidate before deciding.

"From the standpoint of candidacy, this does not hinder anything, because 21 signatures is the minimum," he added. Kivimägi said Isamaa and the Centre Party have until August 21 to give signatures supporting Madise's candidacy.

Kivimägi said his goal is to gather more than 51 signatures by Wednesday evening. "I admit this is not the number needed to be elected in parliament, but getting 51 signatures in a little more than 24 hours is, in my view, quite an impressive statement," he said.

Kivimägi emphasized that he is not convinced whether Isamaa is ready to support any particular presidential candidate in parliament. "Perhaps that will change," he added.

Tiit Land meeting with the Riigikogu Isamaa faction on Wednesday. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Isamaa met Tallinn University of Technology Rector Tiit Land on Wednesday afternoon.

Isamaa chair Urmas Reinsalu said in an interview that the meeting with Land was genuine and honest. "On Monday we will meet with Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise, this time already in the role of a candidate," he added.

Reinsalu said that once Monday's meeting with Madise has taken place, all the most significant candidates will have been heard. After that, Isamaa can make its decision.

Land said that various topics were discussed at the meeting. "We talked a great deal about family policy," he noted. In Land's view, one of the most important issues right now is population decline. "I would do whatever it takes to reverse that trend," he added.

"The proposal from university rectors and the president of the Academy of Sciences for parliament to consider rector Tiit Land for the presidency is a serious signal both to society and to members of the legislature," Isamaa chair Urmas Reinsalu wrote Tuesday on social media. Reinsalu praised Land's readiness to take on presidential responsibility.

The suggestion for Tallinn University of Technology Rector Tiit Land to run for president was made by the rectors of Estonia's universities, Secretary-General of the Rectors' Council Hanna Kanep and President of the Academy of Sciences Mart Saarma.

"I have thought about this seriously and am ready to run if I am nominated. My long leadership experience and recognition in the education and research field encourage me. I have studied and worked abroad, and international communication is not foreign to me," Land wrote Tuesday on social media.

"Using a chemical term, I am neutral for the presidency. I am not a candidate of any single party. The role of president requires sufficiently broad trust. If members of the Riigikogu find that my experience and values could be useful for Estonia in this role, then I am ready to accept that responsibility," added the current rector of Tallinn University of Technology.

The Riigikogu Council of Elders on 11 August. Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

Center Party to form its position after meetings

On Tuesday, the Center Party board met with members of its Riigikogu faction to discuss how to proceed in the presidential election, faction chair Lauri Laats said. They planned to meet with Tiit Land and also wished to speak with Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise.

"We discussed and mapped out where we stand and what possible steps we could take," Laats said. On Wednesday at 15:30 there was a scheduled meeting with Tiit Land. "If additional candidates emerge, we will of course meet with them as well," Laats noted.

Laats said parties have previously met Madise in her role as chancellor of justice, but not as a potential presidential candidate. "We do not know what her vision of the presidency is or how she sees herself in that role," he added.

Once the Center Party chooses its presidential candidate, the party council must be convened. "The board will make a proposal, and the faction will form its position based on that," Laats said. He noted that every Riigikogu member, including Center Party MPs, is free in their vote and will make their decision at the ballot box according to their conscience.

The article has been updated on 12 August with information on the status of signature collection in support of Ülle Madise's candidacy and participants' comments after Isamaa meeting with Tiit Land.

World.title: Fatboy Slim will perform in Estonia for the first time in November
World.content:
Dance music legend Fatboy Slim will perform on November 21 at the Põhjala factory in Tallinn. The artist, appearing in Estonia for the first time, chose the concert venue himself.

Fatboy Slim, whose legal name is Quentin Leo Cook, is a pioneer of dance music whose career took off in the early 1990s. The DJ from the United Kingdom is one of the trailblazers of the big beat genre, and his work played a major role in bringing electronic dance music into the mainstream.

He began his musical path in 1985, not behind a DJ booth but as a bassist in an indie band. Three years later the band broke up, and Cook bought his first controller, synthesizer and sampler. Around the same time he released his first remixes, and "Dub Be Good to Me," released in 1990 by the sound system collective Beats International, which included Cook, reached the top of the charts. Two years later the collective disbanded.

The musician decided to try his hand as a guitarist in an acid jazz band, but he quickly realized he was a poor guitarist. That was followed by Pizzaman, a house music duo with John Reid. Three songs from their only album, "Pizzamania," reached the charts. In 1995 he started the Fatboy Slim project, and the debut album "Better Living Through Chemistry" was released in 1996.

A turning point in Fatboy Slim's career came in 1998 with the release of his second album, "You've Come a Long Way, Baby," which included songs such as "Praise You," "Right Here, Right Now" and "The Rockafeller Skank." He has released four studio albums as Fatboy Slim, the most recent being "Palookaville" in 2004.
